source: The structured effects of the skills the system applies by itself, written out by hand from the Effect text of the Skills tab of the Reference Sheet. The notation is explained at the top of module/rules/skills.mjs. A skill that is not listed is shown with its Effect text only. Where skills of different kinds share a name, each is listed as 'kind.Name' (as 'enemy.Teleport'), which is read before the name alone. 'left' says what part of a listed skill the table still does by hand; a skill with a 'left' counts as partly done. 'note' says how the system reads a skill where its Effect leaves room, or how it is used, with nothing left to do. A skill may have both.

Lethal Grace.note: A critical hit that takes no HP off its target, for whatever reason, deals a tenth of the target's maximum HP instead, rounded down. That damage is no hit of an attack: it can defeat the target, and nothing blocks or lessens it.

Repel.note: Once a fight its unit started is over, the tile behind it lights up on the map: a click on it moves the unit a space straight away from its foe, and a click anywhere else passes. That step is not movement of its own: what it may still move, as with Canto, is counted from the tile it steps onto.

Critical Mastery.note: Critical counts half of DEX, so one and a half times DEX is a further quarter of it.

Nihil.note: The skills it negates are those the reference sheet marks as cancelled by Nihil. Of a foe's skills that are chosen when to activate, what waits to be switched on and what has a moment of the fight does nothing against this unit: they cannot be ticked in the forecast, which says why, one that was switched on beforehand is not spent, and the foe is not offered another weapon.

Ruined Sky.note: A weapon with Flying effectiveness is one whose own Effect says so. The higher multiplier is for attacks against Flying units.

Noncombatant.note: The unit that defeats it earns no experience for that fight.

Brash Assault.note: Read as the unit being at half HP or less.

Sweep.note: Which Sweep it is, and so which stat counts, is picked as the skill is learnt. After every fight its unit starts, and until its next turn starts, it makes no counter-attack against an attacker unless its own stat is 4 or more above the attacker's; both are compared without what skills add.

Offensive Tactics.note: The enemy the unit started a fight against is marked until the Phase ends: every other unit that attacks it meanwhile deals +3 damage, which the forecast counts.

Future Sight.note: The Effect names no duration for the second half: against an attack that would take a quarter or more of the unit's maximum HP off it if it landed without a critical hit, the unit has +10 Dodge and +5 Critical Avoid for each quarter, against that attack, which the forecast counts.

Bloodlust.note: The 5 damage come after a fight the unit began at full HP, whatever it lost in it. The Effect does not call them non-lethal, as Fury's does, so they can defeat the unit.

Armored Boots.note: Read from the unit's HP now rather than at the start of its turn.

Artillerist.note: With Bolts the damage and the Critical are each halved and rounded down.

Critical Focus.note: A unit that has this skill several times picks a different weapon type for each. Of the three Magic types, Anima counts every Anima tome whatever its element, Dark and Light counts Astral as well, and Scrolls and Magicite counts Arcanima and Chaos too. The system has no weapons of the Astral, Scroll, Magicite, Arcanima or Chaos kinds yet, so those count for nothing until it has.

Of the three Magic types, Anima counts every Anima tome whatever its element, Dark and Light counts Astral as well, and Scrolls and Magicite counts Arcanima and Chaos too. Of the three Magic types, Anima counts every Anima tome whatever its element, Dark and Light counts Astral as well, and Scrolls and Magicite counts Arcanima and Chaos too. The system has no weapons of the Astral, Scroll, Magicite, Arcanima or Chaos kinds yet, so those count for nothing until it has.

Cruelty.note: One stat debuff is one of the enemy's stats (STR, MAG, DEX, SPD, LUK, DEF, RES, CON) that is lowered as the fight begins: by a condition, by a change that lasts on it, by an aura, or by a skill of this unit in this fight. A stat lowered by several things counts once.

Opportunist.note: Applied against a foe that makes no counter-attack though its weapon would reach: one that is unarmed or holds a broken weapon, is kept from it by a skill, a condition, Break or Stagger, or cannot answer a Midrange attack; not against one whose weapon simply does not reach. A foe that loses its counter-attack in the middle of the fight gives the bonus from the unit's next attack on. A foe that answers with a Staff gives it from the start.

Pride.note: The bonus for class tiers counts whatever the levels are. A class that does not promote, and a unit without a class, count the tier a promotion would have brought by their level.

Underdog.note: The bonus for class tiers counts whatever the levels are. A class that does not promote, and a unit without a class, count the tier a promotion would have brought by their level.

Unarmed Combat.note: Fists are lent to the unit: it need not carry them. It picks them among its weapons to start a fight with whenever it likes, and with no weapon in its hand it attacks, and attacks back, with them.

Verdant Faith.note: Fists are lent to the unit: it need not carry them. It picks them among its weapons to start a fight with whenever it likes, and with no weapon in its hand it attacks, and attacks back, with them.

Metal Coffin.note: Fists are lent to the unit: it need not carry them. It picks them among its weapons to start a fight with whenever it likes, and with no weapon in its hand it attacks, and attacks back, with them.

Blessing of Vesta.note: Against a foe that wields a Fire tome the unit has Weapon Triangle advantage whatever it wields itself, as long as it has a weapon in hand; the bonus goes by its rank with that weapon.

Radiance.note: The enemy loses 50 Accuracy as the attack lands, from its next attack in that fight on.

Hero's Blood.note: ATK is damage. The boost reaches every ally on the map, counts for the unit from its next attack of that fight, and lasts until the end of the unit's next turn; a follow-up is neither gained nor lost in the middle of a fight.

Blue Flame.note: The allies next to the unit are counted as the attack is made, up to 4. For a unit that is not on a map they cannot be counted, and the skill is named to check by hand.

Burning Desire.note: The effect of the Charm staff is a change that lasts on the target for 3 of its turns, if the attack lands: it stands apart from every side and attacks nobody, from its next attack in that fight on. Burn is inflicted for 3 turns, on top of what the target already has.

Savage.note: The target's DEX is halved as it stands each time it is read, rounded down, from after that fight until the end of its next turn, if the attack lands.

Tear.note: The enemy's LUK counts as 0 for that attack, as the tripled STR does: in its Dodge and its Critical Avoid.

Colossus.note: STR is tripled for a weapon that adds STR. The Might is 1 for each point of CON the unit has more than its target, and counts as the weapon's own.

Synergy.note: MAG and RES are compared as the unit fights with them. The Hit and Dodge count from the start of its next turn to the end of it.

Brutal Strength.note: Half the HP the unit has as the fight begins, rounded down, counts as STR for a weapon that adds STR.

Expiacion.note: On an attack, a third of DEF counts as STR for a weapon that adds STR, and a third of RES as MAG for one that adds MAG. On a hit taken, a third of STR counts as DEF where DEF resists the hit, and a third of MAG as RES where RES does, whatever the weapon. Thirds are rounded down.

Insight.note: The target's DEF and RES are halved as they stand each time they are read, rounded down, from after that fight until the end of this unit's next turn (the turn after this one, where it is in its own turn).

Amplify.note: Might is the number written on the weapon. Of a weapon's Effect the system applies in a fight what it inflicts: for that attack a chance below 100% is half as high again, rounded down (33% to Burn is 49%), and the condition lasts half as many turns again, rounded up (1 turn is 2, 3 turns are 5). What a weapon's Effect says beyond that is text on the weapon for every unit, with or without this skill.

Arcane Blade.note: When it activates the attack is resisted by RES, with what the foe's tile adds to that. It stays what its weapon makes it for Shields and for what asks for a physical or a magical attack.

Corona.note: The target's RES is multiplied by 0.7 as it stands each time it is read, rounded down, from after that fight until the end of its next turn, if the attack lands.

Pounce.note: Once a fight in which Pounce took effect is over, its unit and its foe trade places, if both still stand, each could stand where the other does, and the foe is one that others can move.

Golden Lotus.note: The Dodge is what was taken off the hit. It counts from the next attack of that fight and lasts until the second end of a turn of the unit from then; activated again it is set anew by that hit, not added up.

Holy Vestments.note: What is taken off the hit is added to the damage of the unit's next attack: in the same fight if it still makes one, and otherwise in the next fight in which it attacks, whose forecast counts it.

Misery Mirror.note: The foe loses 5 DEX and SPD at once, for the rest of that fight too, and regains 1 of each as each of its turns starts. Activated again, the loss is back at 5.

Glare.note: Rolled for each attack made against the unit from 2 or 3 spaces, whether it then lands or not; the Stun comes once that attack is made, so the attacker makes no further attack in that fight.

Shieldstrike.note: Each point the 20 take off beyond the damage there was is +1 Hit, Dodge and Critical from the unit's next attack, and the foe's, until the fight ends. A block comes off the hit first.

Scale Shield.note: An attack that targets RES is an attack with a tome. What STR takes off beyond the damage there was is dealt to the attacker, whatever its defence; it can defeat it.

Kestrel.note: The SPD counts for the whole fight in everything it is part of: Attack Speed, and with it Dodge. Where the unit's follow-up, or its foe's, goes by Attack Speed alone, it is gained or lost with it as the fight begins.

Roar.note: Rolled once as the unit starts a fight. The enemy is Stunned at once, before the first attack, so that it makes no counter-attack in that fight.

Iaido.note: For the unit's next attack: in the same fight if it still makes one, and otherwise in the next fight in which it attacks, whose forecast counts it. Carried from one fight to the next it is set anew, not added up.

Punish.note: Applied to every hit taken in a fight in which the unit makes no attack, or in which none of its attacks would deal damage as the fight is planned, whichever unit began it.

Holy Conduit.note: The damage dealt is what the critical hit took off its target. It goes to the ally next to the unit that has lost the most HP; nobody is asked.

Flurry.note: Given for a critical hit in a fight the unit starts in its own turn, if it still stands once the fight is over. It moves again and takes any Action, not only an attack.

Cleave.note: Each hit from next to the target that takes HP off it sends a third of that damage, rounded down, to one other enemy next to the target, picked by a die each time. It is dealt whatever that enemy's defence, as damage a skill deals is, can defeat it, and counts as the unit's kill.

Cold Rain.note: Once a turn: the first hit its unit lands, in whichever fight, from the start of its own turn until its next turn starts. Outside of a battle its use comes back with the Start turn button of the sheet.

Rencounter.note: Each hit landed is +1 END and each attack dodged or blocked +1 ATK, up to +3 each, from after the fight until the end of the unit's next turn. A block with a Shield and one with the weapon in hand both count.

Standardbearer.note: Each attack that lands gives every ally within 2 spaces +2 to one of STR, MAG, DEX, SPD, LUK, DEF and RES, picked by a die for each ally. The same stat again is renewed, not added up; another stat stands beside it.

Onrush.note: The first time on a map that the unit defeats a foe in its own turn: a foe it defeats while another side has its Phase does not use it up. The unit moves and acts again.

Lead by Example.note: In the unit's own turn. Where allies that can be Refreshed stand both next to the unit and next to the foe it defeated, the unit's owner clicks an ally of the group to Refresh; if they do not, the larger group is. Only allies that have acted are Refreshed, as by any Refresh, and a turn in which nobody was is not counted.

Bloodthirst.note: 20% of maximum HP, rounded down, as each of the unit's next three turns starts; over as soon as an attack lands on the unit in a fight the system rolls. Another kill starts the three turns anew.

Fearsome Blow.note: Their HP is maximum HP, a quarter of it rounded down, for every other enemy within 2 spaces of where the defeated enemy stood. It can defeat them, and each one it does is the unit's kill.

Encore.note: The further Action is taken from where the unit stands: it neither attacks, nor uses a Gambit, nor moves, before that Action or after it.

Hook.note: Half the unit's STR without skills, rounded down, from the start of its next turn to the end of it. A kill made during that turn earns nothing for the turn after.

Galeforce.note: Given for a foe the unit defeats in its own turn, by the Action it takes or on its way to it. "Another full action" is read as the games have it: the unit moves and acts again.

Convalescence.note: Half the damage of the first damaging attack to hit the unit since its own turn began, rounded down, is restored as its next turn starts, unless another damaging attack hits it before then. Counted in fights the system rolls.

Runemail.note: +1 MAG for each hit taken and +1 more for one that dealt no damage, up to +8, counted from after the fight and gone as the unit's next turn starts.

Ruse.note: The debuff is 1 larger for each class tier above the first: -4 at Tier 2, -5 at Tier 3 (MOV -3 and -4).

Savage Blow.note: After a fight the unit started and still stands after, every other enemy within 2 spaces of the target takes a fifth of its maximum HP, rounded down, whether or not the target still stands. The target itself takes none. It can defeat them, and each one it does is the unit's kill.

Influence.note: After a fight the unit started and still stands after, every ally next to it regains 7 HP. With Influence the unit's Motivate gives +5 DEF, RES and LUK to allies within 2 spaces and its Rally +6 to one ally or +4 to all within 2 spaces, which are written on Motivate and Rally.

Scorch.note: As the unit starts a fight with a Fire tome in hand, every other enemy next to the target takes Fire damage of the unit's MAG less its own RES, and is Burned whether or not that came to any damage. The target itself is not caught.

Seal.note: Whoever acts for the unit picks the two stats above the dock; with no answer, and for a unit no player owns, the two the enemy has the most of are taken. For 1 turn is until the end of the enemy's next turn.

Hit and Run.note: Rolled after a fight the unit started. The move is of its whole MOV from where it stands, whatever it had spent, and the HP is regained once the move stands: as the unit Waits or its Phase ends. An enemy with Constraint curbs it as it does Canto.

Raucous Roar.note: Rolled after a fight the unit started and survived, at most until it has taken effect twice in a turn. The unit moves and acts again with its whole MOV, unless something keeps it from being Refreshed. The HST lasts until its turn ends.

Mug.note: The amount is what the Game Master set: the Gold the enemy carries on its sheet, all of which is taken, or, for an enemy that carries none, the world's setting "Gold stolen from an enemy that carries none" (50 unless changed). It is given through the same door as any gold, so it floats over the unit. Once it has taken effect against an enemy it is not rolled against that enemy again on that map. Nothing is taken from a unit that cannot be stolen from.

Despoil.note: The Bullion of the Items tab is put in the unit's pack, and its name floats over the unit. An enemy brought to 0 HP by hand counts as defeated by the unit selected on the map.

Bargain.note: In the Market of the Base every price shown to the unit that is buying is the price it pays, with what was taken off on hover. Discounts add up: with a Bargain Ring equipped the unit pays half. A price is rounded down. What a unit sells for does not change.

Plunder.note: With Greed on the unit as well it pays 100 Gold for each level. An enemy brought to 0 HP by hand counts as defeated by the unit selected on the map.

Robbery.note: The D3 is rolled by the system. On a 1 the Game Master is shown the fallen enemy's pack and picks the item the unit gains, or none; with no Game Master at the table, or no answer in 30 seconds, a die picks among the items that are not equipped or worn. On a 2 the gold is what the Game Master set, as for Mug: the Gold the enemy carries, or the world's setting for an enemy that carries none. On a 3 a Bullion is put in the unit's pack. What is gained floats over the unit. Nothing but the Bullion is gained from a unit that cannot be stolen from.

Forager.note: On the move a unit makes after its Action a space of Forest, Thicket or Wardwood takes 1 movement, as open ground does.

Omen.note: As each of the unit's turns starts a die picks one enemy on the map, which is Rattled and carries the skill's mark for as long as that Rattle lasts. When the unit defeats an enemy that carries its mark, by an attack or otherwise, every enemy on the map is Rattled. An enemy that cannot be targeted is passed over.

Holy Aura.note: Their HP is maximum HP, a fifth of it rounded down, for every ally within 3 spaces. The unit itself is not healed.

Bewitch.note: Rolled as each of the unit's turns starts; its Use button forces the effect without a roll and starts the cooldown of 4 turns, which takes no Action. Every enemy next to the unit is Berserked until the end of its next turn, and for as long as that lasts it can make the target of an attack, a staff or a skill neither one of its enemies (the unit and the unit's allies) nor another unit Bewitched so: the map does not offer them.

Invincible.note: That turn runs from the start of its unit's turn to the start of its next, so through the Phases of the other sides: it takes no damage of any kind meanwhile. Once it has taken effect it is not rolled as its unit's next turn starts.

Lottery.note: A die says how many of the six stats are boosted (1 to 3), dice pick which, and each is boosted by a die of its own (1 to 5), until the end of that turn.

Sharpen Claws.note: Waits for the next fight in which the unit makes an attack, and counts for its first attack there, whose forecast shows it. Activated again before then it is renewed, not added up.

Shade.note: Until its unit's next turn starts, while the Phase of any side but the players' is running, no enemy can make it the target of an attack, a staff or a skill used on a unit: the map does not offer it, and the Attack button refuses. What an enemy's skill does to the units around passes it over as well: a spread, a change for the units in reach, an aura, the curse of a song. Outside of a battle there are no Phases, and it does nothing.

Shatter.note: The -5 DEF and RES and the 20 uses off the target's Shield come if the attack lands; the uses are taken once the fight is over.

Umbra.note: The unit loses half its HP, rounded down and never its last, as the fight the skill is used for begins. The damage and the Poison last for 1 turn afterwards, in which no further fight halves its HP.

Capote.note: When an attack against the unit would hit, whoever acts for it is offered the dodge in the middle of the fight, once the hit and its critical are rolled and with the damage it would deal: one click takes it, and no answer within 15 seconds leaves it. The attack then misses, as a dodge does for everything that waits for one, and the cooldown starts. Passing costs nothing.

Flee.note: In a fight the unit started, with more Attack Speed than its foe, whoever acts for it is offered to end the fight each time the foe is about to attack, with the Hit and damage of that attack. Taken, the fight ends there: that attack and everything after it are not made, the unit earns no experience from the fight (its foe earns what it earned), and the cooldown starts. It is not offered before the unit's own attacks.

Gigas Grip.note: Ticked in the forecast of an attack, or switched on beforehand for a fight in which the unit is attacked, which then spends it. Its weapon and its Shield weigh nothing as Attack Speed is worked out, and so for the Dodge that is counted from it.

Hustle.note: Used from the skill list before the unit moves; using it is no Action. The price comes whether or not the second Action is taken: from the end of that turn the unit has -3 to STR, MAG, DEX, SPD, LUK, DEF, RES and CON (not HP or MOV), loses its following turn, and is itself again as the turn after that starts.

Singular Strike.note: Ticked in the forecast, or switched on beforehand for a fight in which the unit is attacked. "Base damage" is the unit's Atk before the foe's defence. The attacks it would make count each strike of a weapon that strikes twice, its follow-up and the attacks its skills add. A unit that would make one attack anyway gains nothing, and the skill is not spent.

Stunt.note: Ticked in the forecast: the first attack of the unit that lands in the fight counts as a critical hit for its skills that wait for one, without the damage of one. A fight in which none of its attacks lands does not spend it.

Spellshield.note: Switched on from the Skill list of the dock in the unit's own turn, which takes no Action: whoever acts for the unit picks the tome from a short list of the basic tomes of the kinds of magic it has a rank of E or higher with (Force, Fire, Thunder, Wind, Water, Ice, Stone, Light, Flux), each with its numbers from the Weapons tab; a unit no player owns takes the one with the most Might. The skill then stays on, fight after fight, until its unit is hit: that hit deals a quarter less, and if the unit still stands the tome is cast at the attacker at once, with the tome's numbers at -10 Hit and half its damage, from as far as the tome reaches and no nearer than it does, whatever the unit holds and whether or not its own weapon could answer. It costs nothing and is not answered. The fight in which it was hit spends the skill, which then sits out 3 turns.

Animus.note: The seven tomes are listed with the unit's own weapons in the dock, marked with the skill: Force, Fire, Wind, Thunder, Water, Ice and, for Earth, Stone, each with its numbers from the Weapons tab. One that is taken up is what the unit starts its next fight with, whatever is in its hand and whatever its ranks: it has no uses to lose, cannot be traded or put away, and earns half the tome's weapon experience. That fight is the use of the skill, which then sits out 3 turns, during which the tomes are greyed with the turns left. A tome that was taken up and not attacked with is put down again as the unit acts. Counter-attacks are made with the weapon in hand.

Animose.note: The seven tomes are listed with the unit's own weapons in the dock, marked with the skill: Surge, Blaze, Draft, Charge, Tide, Chill and Fissure, each with its numbers from the Weapons tab, so that Chill attacks at Midrange only. One that is taken up is what the unit starts its next fight with, whatever is in its hand and whatever its ranks: it has no uses to lose, cannot be traded or put away, and earns half the tome's weapon experience. That fight is the use of the skill, which then sits out 3 turns, during which the tomes are greyed with the turns left. A tome that was taken up and not attacked with is put down again as the unit acts. Counter-attacks are made with the weapon in hand.

Body Blow.note: Ticked in the forecast. "Base damage" is the unit's Atk before the foe's defence, worked out with the higher of DEF and RES in place of STR for a weapon that adds STR; a weapon that adds another stat keeps it. A unit that would make one attack anyway gains nothing, and the skill is not spent.

Throw.note: Once a fight its unit started is over in which it landed 2 attacks, the free tiles next to the unit light up, and its foe: a click on a tile sets the foe down there, deals it 5 damage and Dazes it, with a cooldown of 3 turns; a click on the foe itself deals the damage and the Daze without moving it, with a cooldown of 1 turn; a click anywhere else passes, and the skill is not used. A foe that is not moved by others is only offered the second.

Tools of the Trade.note: As a battle begins, whoever acts for the unit has the Compendium opened at the Buffing and Combat items, each with a Make button while it still fits the cost that is left; the same item may be made twice, and closing the window ends the picking. Each item has DEX/10 uses, rounded down and 1 at least, is marked as made by the skill, and is gone as the battle ends, used or not, from whichever pack it is in by then. A unit no player owns makes the costliest items that fit by itself.

Juna Oil.note: Used from the skill list before the unit moves; it lasts until the unit's next turn, and using it is not the unit's Action. WT is the unit's Weight, and an eighth of it is dealt to each enemy moved through, shares of a point dropped. Used while on cooldown it gives +1 MOV, the unit is given Burn for a turn at once, and the 3 turns of cooldown start again.

Fulmination.note: Ticked in the forecast for a fight the unit starts. Before the first attack every other enemy within 3 spaces of the target takes Dark damage of the unit's MAG, whatever its defence, and is left with 1 HP at the least. The target itself is not caught. The fight spends the skill.

Rebuke.note: As a hit would land on an ally next to its unit that deals at least half the HP the ally has left, in a fight the system rolls, whoever acts for the unit is offered, in one click, to negate it: the ally takes nothing, and half of what it would have taken, rounded down, is dealt to the attacker at once, whatever its defence, which can defeat it and end the fight. A unit no player owns always does. The cooldown of 3 turns starts when it is used. Damage that is no attack of a fight is not answered.

Fast Fingers.note: A melee attack is one made from next to the foe, in a fight its unit starts or is attacked in. Once such a fight is over in which one landed, whoever acts for the unit is shown the foe's pack above the dock, as for Steal: a click takes one item that is not equipped or worn, and no weapon heavier than the unit's STR; the test of SPD is the Steal action's and is not asked. The cooldown of 4 turns starts when an item is taken; passing, or a foe with nothing to take, uses nothing. A unit no player owns takes the item that costs the most. Nothing is taken from a unit that cannot be stolen from.

Cannon.note: Used from the Skill list with a Bolt in hand that attacks (one with a Hit of its own, not one that places something): the tiles the Bolt reaches light up in violet, the 3x3 square follows the pointer with the damage and the Hit of the attack over every enemy in it, and a click on a tile or an enemy places it. Each enemy in the square is then attacked once, rolled by itself and shown over its unit, with no counter-attack and no follow-up; the card has a row for each. The Bolt loses one use for the whole volley. Every enemy that was attacked, hit or missed, then has -10 Dodge and Hit, -2 DEF and RES and -2 damage until the end of its next turn. With any other weapon in hand the skill cannot be used. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Fatality.note: Ticked in the forecast, for the first attack the unit makes in the fight, as every skill declared before rolling to hit is. That attack deals effective damage whatever the foe is, unless a skill of the foe negates effective damage, and if it lands it counts as a critical hit for the unit's skills that wait for one, without the damage of one.

Primal Fury.note: The temporary HP come as the skill is used and go with it, as the unit's third turn after that starts; they are lost before its own.

Fortress.note: While it lasts nothing moves the unit but the unit itself: it is not offered to a Shove, a swap or a staff that moves a unit, friend or foe, stays where it is when units around it are pushed, and is held but not dragged by a unit that grapples it.

Immolation.note: Picked from the Skill list, the tiles within 2 spaces of the unit are painted with the Burn each unit there would be given; a click on the area or the Confirm button uses it, a click anywhere else calls it off. Every unit in it, friend or foe, and the unit itself are given 2 turns of Burn, which add to a Burn they already have. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Provoke.note: For 3 of its turns the enemy can make no other enemy of its own the target of an attack, a staff or a skill than the unit: the map does not offer them and says why when one is clicked. It ends with the first fight that enemy is in, whoever started it, and holds only while the unit stands on the map. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Unnerve.note: Picked from the Skill list, the tiles within 2 spaces of the unit are painted and every enemy there is marked; a click on the area or the Confirm button Rattles them all, a click anywhere else calls it off. An enemy that cannot be targeted is passed over. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Breath Weapon.note: The Anima type is picked as the skill is learnt: Anima, Fire, Thunder, Wind, Water, Ice or Earth. From then on the Arc- tome of that type with a Range of 1-2 on the Weapons tab (Arcforce, Arcfire, Arcthunder, Arcwind, Arcwater, Arcice, Arcstone) is listed with the unit's own weapons in the dock, marked with the skill. Taken up, it is what the unit starts its next fight with, at 1-2 range and with MAG, whatever is in its hand: an attack like any other, which the foe answers where its weapon reaches. It has no uses to lose and earns no weapon experience. That fight is the use of the skill, which then sits out 3 turns. It is not lent to a unit that has dismounted, which no unit has until the Dismounting Optional Module is built.

Hemorrhage.note: The damage is a tenth of the enemy's maximum HP, rounded down and 1 at least, dealt as a skill's damage is (whatever its defence; it can defeat). For 2 of its turns the enemy then loses 1 HP each time it moves of its own accord, and 1d4 HP after each fight in which it made an attack; either can defeat it, as the unit's kill. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Blast.note: Used before the unit moves; it is the unit's Action. From the start of its next turn to the end of that turn every Tome has +6 Might, and a Tome whose own Range ends at 3 or less reaches 2 spaces further, which the map paints. The cooldown of 3 turns starts as it is used.

Foul Play.note: Picked from the unit's menu on the map: the allies it may trade places with light up, and a click on one swaps the two. An ally is offered within 5 spaces where a straight line between the two crosses no Wall tile and no wall of the scene, and each could stand where the other does. Off a battle map the skill is only counted.

Enlighten.note: The unit itself and the allies next to it light up, those with a skill that rolls a chance to activate in a fight. A die picks one such skill of the unit clicked, which is named over it: in the next fight that unit is in, that skill activates whenever its moment comes. The guarantee is used up by that fight and gone with the map. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Waterwheel.note: Picked from the Skill list, the eight tiles around the unit are painted, diagonals included, and every unit on them shows the damage and the Hit of the attack it would take; a click on the area or the Confirm button makes the attacks, a click anywhere else calls it off. "All units" is read as written: allies around the unit are attacked as well as enemies. Each is attacked once with the weapon in hand, whatever its range, rolled by itself and shown over its unit, with no counter-attack and no follow-up; the card has a row for each. The weapon loses one use for the whole action. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Sabotage.note: The enemies within 3 spaces light up; once one is clicked, whoever acts for the unit picks the stat from a list above the dock (STR, MAG, DEX, SPD, LUK, DEF or RES). With no answer, and for a unit no player owns, the stat that enemy has the most of is lowered. It lasts until the unit's own next turn starts. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Howl.note: Picked from the Skill list, the tiles within 2 spaces of the unit are painted and every enemy there is marked; a click on the area or the Confirm button Stuns them all, a click anywhere else calls it off. An enemy that cannot be targeted is passed over. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Death Grip.note: Picked from the unit's menu on the map and used on an enemy next to it: both roll d100 and add their bonus, the unit to Athletics and the foe to the better of Reflex and Athletics, and the unit takes hold unless the foe's total is higher. A foe that is held cannot move, act or dodge, and is dragged to the tile behind its holder as that unit moves. The check is rolled again as each of the foe's turns starts, and the foe may use its Action to roll it once more (Break Free, in its menu). The hold ends when the foe wins the check, when the two no longer stand next to each other, when either leaves the fight, or when the holder lets go by picking the skill again; the cooldown of 3 turns starts then. A check that fails at once starts it at once.

Confiteor.note: The enemies within 3 spaces light up; a click opens the forecast and confirming rolls one attack whose damage before defence is the unit's STR + MAG, resisted by the lower of the target's DEF and RES. It has the Hit of the weapon in hand (0 unarmed) with the unit's own DEX and LUK, costs that weapon no use, has no weapon triangle and nothing of the weapon's Effect, is not answered and has no follow-up. It is the unit's attack for the turn. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Override.note: Picked from the Skill list, the enemies next to the unit that it can charge through light up in violet; with the pointer on one, the line is painted through it and every enemy standing right behind it, one after the other, with the damage each would take and the way the unit goes. A click makes one attack on each with the weapon in hand: it cannot miss, is not answered, and none of the unit's skills takes effect at a moment of it. The unit then moves through them onto the first tile past the last, which must be one it can stand on with no unit on it and no wall in the way: a line without such a tile is not offered. Lines run along rows and columns. The weapon loses one use for the whole action. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Smoke Bomb.note: Picked from the Skill list, the tiles 1 to 3 spaces from the unit light up in violet: the bomb lands on the one that is clicked, and the tiles within 2 spaces of it are painted as the pointer moves, with every enemy they would catch marked. Accuracy is Hit. Each enemy caught has -30 Hit and Dodge and half its MOV, rounded down, until the end of its next turn. A click on a tile where nobody would be caught does nothing; a click anywhere else calls it off. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Lunar Cry.note: Picked from the Skill list, the tiles within 4 spaces of the unit are painted, every enemy there is marked, and the unit shows how many times over it would gain; a click on the area or the Confirm button uses it. The enemies are counted as the skill is used: the unit has +2 STR, DEX, SPD and DEF for each, and each of them -2. Both last until the unit's third turn from now starts. With no enemy in reach the skill is not used. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Malaise.note: Picked from the Skill list, the enemies next to the unit light up; a click gives one of them Malaise for 3 turns. Malaise is a condition of its own: -4 DEX and SPD, and 10% of maximum HP, rounded down, lost as each of its unit's turns starts. While it lasts, that unit's allies within 3 spaces of it have -2 DEX and SPD, and each loses 10% of its own maximum HP once in each of its turns: as the turn starts where it stands that near then, or else as the turn ends where it has come that near. Several afflicted units nearby count once. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Cheer.note: The stat is picked as the skill is learnt. Picked from the Skill list, a short list asks for one ally (+4) or all adjacent allies (+2); for one, the allies next to the unit light up and a click gives the bonus. For 1 turn is until the unit's own next turn starts. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Deathmatch.note: Picked from the Skill list, it offers the enemies the weapon in hand reaches from where the unit stands that can counter-attack it. A click opens the forecast, which says 5 rounds and shows the HP both would have left; confirming fights 5 rounds as one fight, each with its own dice, which ends early when a unit falls or when a round passes in which nobody could attack. It is the unit's attack for the turn.

Jeer.note: The stat is picked as the skill is learnt. Picked from the Skill list, a short list asks for one enemy (-4) or all adjacent enemies (-2); for one, the enemies next to the unit light up and a click lowers the stat. For 1 turn is until the end of that enemy's next turn. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Maneuver.note: Picked from the unit's menu on the map: the allies next to it light up, and once one is picked, the tiles to choose from. A click on the ally itself trades places with it, on a tile next to the ally moves the unit there, and on a tile next to the unit sets the ally down there. Off a battle map the skill is only counted.

Overwatch.note: Used as an action, its unit Holds until its next turn starts, with a shield on its token and a chip on its dock. Once in that time, as an enemy moves in its own turn through, into or out of a tile the weapon in the unit's hand attacks from where it stands, the enemy is stopped on the first such tile it can stand on (before it has moved at all, if it sets out from one) and whoever acts for the unit is offered the fight in one click; a unit no player owns takes it. The unit starts that fight as any other, and the enemy counter-attacks if it can. An enemy that lost HP in it cannot move for the rest of its turn; one that lost none walks on. A unit its enemies do not see is not reacted to. Canto does not follow the skill. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Pebble.note: The enemies 2 or 3 spaces away light up; a click opens the forecast of the throw, and confirming rolls it. The stone is a physical attack made with its own numbers in place of a weapon's (Might 0, Hit 50, Critical 5, the unit's STR, DEX and LUK as ever): one attack that is not answered, with no follow-up, no weapon triangle and no use of the weapon in hand, at which none of the unit's skills activates. If it lands, 50% to Stun. It is the unit's attack for the turn. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Protect.note: Used as an action, its unit stands guard, with a filled shield on its token and a chip on its dock, until it is moved by anything or no ally stands next to it, and no longer than the map. While it does, an enemy that starts a fight with an ally next to it fights the unit instead: the enemy's forecast shows the unit as its target, and the fight is fought at the distance to the ally and on the ally's ground, with the unit's own numbers. Nobody is asked. One attack a skill makes, a staff and a Gambit are no fight an enemy starts. Where several units stand guard for one ally, the first of them fights. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Salve.note: The unit itself and the allies next to it light up, those that have lost HP: a click restores 5 HP. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Avert.note: Used as an action, its unit Holds until its next turn starts, as with Overwatch, and reacts once in that time: to an enemy that moves through, into or out of a tile its weapon attacks, and to one that comes within 2 spaces. Whoever acts for it is offered the fight in one click; a unit no player owns takes it. Where its weapon does not reach the enemy from where it stands, the unit first moves to the tile nearest to it from which the weapon does, within its movement. After the fight the enemy cannot move for the rest of its turn, whether it lost HP or not. Canto does not follow the skill. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Sacrifice.note: Picked from the Skill list, the tiles within 5 spaces of the unit are painted and the allies there that lack HP, or points of a Shift Gauge, light up in green. A click on an ally gives it all it lacks, as far as the unit can pay, and a second click takes that share away again; Shift-click adds 2, Ctrl-click takes 2 off, Alt-click restores its Shift Gauge in place of its HP. What each ally would gain and what the unit would lose show over them, 1 HP for every 2 restored, part of one paid in full. The Confirm button or a click on the unit itself uses it. The unit keeps 1 HP at the least. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Spell Trap.note: Used as an action with a Tome in hand: the free tiles next to its unit light up, and a click lays the trap on one, for one use of that Tome. The trap is shown on its tile to the unit's side and to the Game Master, and not to its enemies. Any other unit that moves onto the tile in its own turn, friend or foe, is stopped there, cannot move for the rest of its turn, and is attacked once by the unit with that Tome as it was when the trap was laid, from wherever the unit stands, without a counter-attack and at no further use; the trap is then gone. A third trap takes the place of the oldest. Traps go with the battle, and with a unit that leaves the map. A unit that is shoved or warped onto a trap does not spring it. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Haymaker.note: Only for a unit that carries a Brawl weapon it may wield and that is not broken: the first in its pack is used, whatever it holds. The enemies next to it light up; a click opens the forecast and confirming rolls one attack with that weapon at half its final damage, which is not answered, strikes once and has no follow-up, and costs that weapon a use as any attack with it. If it lands, 15% to Daze, 25% for a unit of Tier 3; the chance is as written, whatever the unit's Skill Activation rate. It is the unit's attack for the turn. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Mark.note: Every enemy on the map lights up; a click marks it for the rest of the map, and the mark is taken off the enemy marked before. Whoever fights the marked enemy has +15 Hit and Critical and +3 damage against it, the unit itself included, which the forecast counts. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Camouflage.note: Used as an action by a unit that stands on a Forest or a Thicket: until its next turn starts its enemies do not see it. Its token is not shown to them, none of them can make it the target of an attack, a staff or a skill, and it is not in their way on the map. An enemy whose move would take it onto the unit's tile stops on the tile before it, and whoever acts for the unit picks in one click: one attack on that enemy, which is not answered and ends the effect, or a move of up to half its MOV, rounded down, to a tile picked on the map, after which the enemy walks on. With neither, the enemy goes no further that way. The effect also ends as soon as the unit makes any attack, or stands on a tile that is neither Forest nor Thicket. A unit no player owns attacks. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Sentry.note: Used as an action, its unit Holds until its next turn starts. In that time it may start a fight with every enemy that moves in its own turn through, into or out of a tile its weapon attacks, once with each enemy: whoever acts for it is offered each fight in one click, and a unit no player owns takes every one. The enemy is stopped where the fight is fought and walks on afterwards. A unit that also has Overwatch equipped fights these with +10 Hit and +2 damage, and once in that time may end the move of the enemy it reacts to: the offer then reads "Attack and end its move" beside "Attack", and a unit no player owns ends the move of the first. Canto does not follow the skill. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Rally.note: Picked from the Skill list, a short list asks for one ally (+4) or all adjacent allies (+2). Whoever acts for each ally picks its stat from a list above the dock on their own map; with no answer in 15 seconds, and for an ally no player owns, the stat it has the most of is raised. For 1 turn is until the unit's own next turn starts. For a unit that also has Influence equipped the bonuses are +6 and +4 and reach allies within 2 spaces. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Harsh Command.note: The ally carries the command until the end of its turn (this one if it has yet to act, else its next). While it does, every penalty to STR, MAG, DEX, SPD, LUK, DEF, RES or CON that a condition, a change another unit left on it or an aura puts on it counts as a bonus of the same size; penalties to damage, Hit, Dodge, Critical and Critical Avoid from those are negated, so that it receives none from skills such as Daunt or Intimidate; no enemy holds it in place, lowers its MOV or stops it beside a unit; and it makes its counter-attack whatever skill or condition would keep it from one. A condition that keeps a unit from moving by itself still does. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Forward Observation.note: Every enemy on the map lights up; a click chooses it for the rest of the map, in place of the enemy chosen before. Whoever fights it has +15 Dodge and +2 DEF and RES against it. Line of Sight is the unit's LoS stat, read as so many spaces. It is looked at as the skill is used and as each of the chosen enemy's turns starts: the first time it stands within the unit's LoS it has -15 Hit until the end of its next turn; each of its turns that starts there adds -5 Hit and -1 damage, up to 10 times over, and a turn that starts outside takes all of that off. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Art of War.note: Until the unit's own next turn starts the ally has +10 Critical, +20 Hit and +3 damage with one kind of weapon (Critical Focus, Weapon Focus, Weaponfaire), picked by a die among the proficiencies that ally has a rank in, and +15 Hit and Dodge, +3 damage and +10 Critical against one kind of weapon (Weaponbreaker, Weaponkiller), picked by a die among the kinds its enemies on the map hold. One kind is picked for the first three and one for the last two. A unit with a rank of B or higher in a proficiency is asked, for each of the two, whether to pick one of those proficiencies in place of the die; a unit no player owns takes the die. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

To the Death.note: Picked from the Skill list, it offers the enemies the weapon in hand reaches from where the unit stands that can counter-attack it. Confirming the forecast fights round after round as one fight, each with its own dice, until a unit falls; it also ends when a round passes in which nobody could attack, and after 50 rounds at the latest. It is the unit's attack for the turn.

Run.note: While Run is on, a unit that has used any of the 3 MOV it adds can do nothing but Wait, and Run stays on until its move is taken back or its next turn.

Fury.note: Switched on, it counts in every fight the unit is in, and the 5 damage come after each of them, leaving the unit 1 HP at the least.

Blood Tide.note: Used from the Skill list, which takes no Action: every ally on the map lights up and a click chooses one. The unit and that ally both have +2 STR and +4 DEX for the rest of the map; used on another ally, the first loses it. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Wave The Flag.note: Flag stance is switched on and off from the skill list.

Pulverize.note: DEF and RES are a quarter of what they are from the start of the fight until the unit makes its follow-up attack, and for the whole fight where it makes none; the forecast counts the foe's attacks before and after that apart.

Robust.note: Switched on beforehand for the next fight the unit is in, or ticked in the forecast of its own attack; that fight spends it. "Their HP" is maximum HP: a hit takes no more than 45% of it, rounded down, off the unit. Damage that is no hit of an attack is not held back.

Master Horseman.note: +3 MOV for the rest of the turn it is used in, +2 in its unit's next turn and +1 in the one after. Used again before that it starts over at +3, and does not add up.

Odds Manipulator.note: When an attack roll of the unit misses, by whatever margin, whoever acts for it is offered to roll again; each roll made again is one of the 4 uses. It rolls an attack again once: a new roll that misses is left, unless another skill of the unit may roll it again. Passing costs nothing.

Dogma.note: Picked from the Skill list, every ally on the map is marked; a click on one of them or the Confirm button uses it. Each has its Skill Activation rate raised by the unit's LUK, as that stands when the skill is used, until the unit's next turn starts. As that turn starts, whoever acts for the unit is asked above its dock whether to extend it: the unit then loses a quarter of its maximum HP, rounded down, which can defeat it, the allies have the bonus for one more turn, and for that turn the unit can only move and Wait. It is asked again each turn it was extended; an extension is no use of the skill. A unit no player owns that answers by itself lets it end. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Holy War.note: Used from the Skill list once a map, in any turn of the unit, without taking its Action: its Effect does not call it an action. Every enemy on the map with a rank in Dark magic or the Terror quality is marked on the map; a click on one of them or the Confirm button uses it. Each has -3 STR, MAG, DEF and RES until the end of its third turn, and the unit has +3 to the same four in every fight against one of them for the rest of the map, which the forecast counts. With no such enemy on the map the skill is not used. Off a battle map it is only counted.

Battery.note: Switched on from the Skill list of the dock, or ticked in a forecast: while it is on, the Tome in hand also attacks from 3 to 10 spaces, which the map shows, and from nearer only as far as it reaches by itself. A fight the unit starts from further than the Tome reaches by itself spends the skill; one from nearer leaves it on. The first such fight of a map costs nothing more. Every later one that map is fought at -25 Hit and Critical and starts a cooldown of 3 turns, and the skill says so on the sheet once its use is spent. The foe counter-attacks where its own weapon reaches.

Deflect Arrows.note: A ranged attack is one made from 2 spaces or more, with whatever weapon. Before each such attack against the unit is rolled, whoever acts for it is offered the +15 Dodge with the Hit and damage of that attack; taken, it counts for that attack alone and the use is spent until the unit's next turn starts. A unit that also has Snatch Arrows is offered that in its place.

Snatch Arrows.note: A ranged attack is one made from 2 spaces or more, with whatever weapon. Before each such attack against the unit is rolled, whoever acts for it is offered to negate it, with the Hit and damage of that attack. A negated attack is made and does nothing: nothing is rolled for it, it is neither a hit nor a miss, and a weapon that wears with every attack still loses its use. The use comes back as the unit's next turn starts.

Sidearm.note: When an enemy attacks the unit, whoever acts for it is offered the other weapons in its pack that it may wield, above the dock on their own map, before the fight is rolled: one click changes weapon, Pass or no answer in 20 seconds keeps the one in hand. Its two uses come back as the unit's own turn starts. Nothing is offered to a unit with no other weapon, nor against a foe with Nihil.

Redirect.note: Once a turn, as a hit that deals damage would land on an ally next to its unit in a fight the system rolls, whoever acts for the unit is offered, in one click, to take it: the ally takes nothing of that hit, and the unit takes its damage worked out again with its own DEF or RES in place of the ally's, as an attack of the unit that made it (which defeats the unit if that brings it down). The offer names the damage it would take. A unit no player owns takes a hit that would not defeat it where that hit would defeat the ally or takes less off it than off the ally. Damage that is no attack of a fight is not answered.

Alarm.note: Three times a turn, as the move an enemy makes in its own turn takes it from outside onto a tile its unit could move to from where it stands, every ally that stands on such a tile gains +2 DEF and RES, +10 Dodge and +5 Critical Avoid against that enemy until the Phase that is running ends. It is given by itself to the first three enemies that come in, where at least one ally stands in that range; the unit itself is no ally of its own. Off a battle map it does nothing.

Suppress.note: Twice a turn, in any Phase: once a fight is over in which an enemy took HP off an ally of its unit, and that enemy still stands on a tile the weapon in the unit's hand attacks from where it stands, whoever acts for the unit is offered one attack on it in one click; a unit no player owns makes it. The attack is not answered, strikes once without a follow-up, and costs the weapon a use. An attack on the unit itself is no attack on an ally; neither a Gambit nor one attack a skill makes is a fight.

Aquila.note: Against an enemy next to an ally of the unit, on either side of a fight: a unit that would not follow up does, and one that follows up by its own Attack Speed makes one more attack after all others. The forecast counts both.

Honor Among Thieves.note: Steal refuses its unit and says why, and a skill that takes an item or gold from a foe in a fight takes nothing from it.

Harmonize.note: Counted are the allies within 2 spaces that carry at least one Tome, not broken, which they may wield by their own ranks. For a unit that is not on a map they cannot be counted, and the skill is named to check by hand.

Loyalty.note: Used from the Skill list once a map, which takes no Action: every ally on the map lights up and a click chooses one for that map. While the chosen ally stands within 2 spaces the unit has +10 Hit and Critical. The choice can be made in any of the unit's turns, not only the first. Off a battle map nothing of it is judged.

Spotting.note: Counted in every fight on a battle map, and in the forecast: against an enemy that at least one ally of the unit has in its Line of Sight, +3 damage, +15 Hit and +10 Critical where the fight is at 5 spaces or more, and +1, +10 and +5 where it is at 4 or less. An ally has an enemy in its Line of Sight when the enemy stands no further away than the ally's LoS counts spaces and no Wall tile or wall of the scene lies between them; an enemy in a Thicket is only seen from next to it. Off a battle map nothing is added.

Giant Swing.note: The MOV left is the unit's MOV less the movement it took to reach the tile it attacks from. A unit that has yet to move has all of it left.

Momentum.note: The spaces moved are those of the way from where the unit's turn began to the tile it attacks from. Half a point is rounded down.

Adieu.note: The tiles are the spaces of the move made after the unit's Action, whichever skill granted it, counted by the way taken. They count until the unit's next turn starts.

Agility.note: The MOV left is the unit's MOV less the movement it took to reach the tile it attacks from.

Hastilude.note: The next attack is the first attack of the fight the unit starts in the turn it moved. Half a point is rounded down, and a Hasta adds its own Might for each space moved on top.

Leonine Lunge.note: The MOV left is the unit's MOV less the movement it took to reach the tile it attacks from.

Charge.note: A full movement is one that leaves the unit no MOV.

Moxie.note: Before moving is from the tile the unit's turn began on.

Outrider.note: Counted as the unit moves, and kept once its turn is over until its next turn starts.

Natural Cover.note: Terrain with an effect is a tile that gives or takes DEF, RES or Dodge, heals, or takes more movement than open ground. For a Flying unit only a tile that heals is.

Terrain Fighter.note: The terrain type is a row of the terrain table, picked as the skill is learnt. A Flying unit stands on a kind of terrain like any other.

options.hint: House, Shop, Village: +1 ATK, +1 END, +3 Hit
Plain, Road, Snow, Sand, Floor: +1 HST
A space of either takes 3 movement at most. +2 END on either
Water, Sea, Ocean and River: no movement penalty for Rivers. +2 HST on either
Fort, Throne, Gate: +1 ATK, +1 END, +5 Hit and Critical
Desert, Dune: +2 RES, +5 Hit and Critical Avoid
Regains 10% more HP at the start of its turn

Sojourner.note: Mountain & Cliff and Water & River change what those tiles take a unit that can cross them, as a Brigand's Mountaineer or a Pirate's Privateer lets it; they do not open them to a unit that cannot. The 10% of Healhedge is regained beside what the tile itself heals.

Forester.note: What the foe's tile adds to its DEF, RES and Dodge is negated. What the foe's own skills give it for standing there is not.

Open Assault.note: Terrain without any effects is a tile that gives or takes nothing, heals nothing and takes no more movement than open ground: Plain, Road, Snow, Sand, Floor. For a Flying unit every tile that does not heal is.

Pathfinder.note: The +2 MOV is for the turn that starts on such a tile, wherever the unit moves to, and ends with that turn.

Altesse.note: An ally's gender is read from the Gender typed on its sheet. An ally of neither gender benefits whatever was chosen, and so does one with nothing typed.

Advisor.note: Tomes and staves are magical ranks, every other proficiency a physical one. An ally without any weapon rank does not benefit.

Authority.note: On promoting, the promotion dialog offers to raise Authority in place of the Promotion or Mastery Skill: +10 to both boosts, or one more Leadership Star with the Authority & Leadership module. The stars count with those typed on the sheet.

Vindication.note: The first time in a Phase that an enemy starts a fight against an ally within 2 spaces, that ally has +2 END in the fight and the unit gains +3 ATK (damage) until the end of its next turn. Nothing more comes of it until that Phase is over.

Motivate.note: For a unit that also has Influence equipped the bonuses are 2 higher and reach allies within 2 spaces.

Divine Authority.note: With the Authority & Leadership module the 3 Leadership Stars count with those typed on the sheet.

Ploy.note: Whoever acts for the unit picks the stat above the dock as its turn starts; with no answer, and for a unit no player owns, the stat those enemies have the most of is taken. It is one of STR, MAG, DEF, RES, SPD, DEX and LUK, RES is compared as it stands, and the end of the turn is the end of the Phase that is running.

Staredown.note: Enemies that start their turn within 2 spaces have -2 MOV for that turn by themselves. As an action, picked from the Skill list: every tile the unit has in its Line of Sight is painted and each enemy on them is marked; a click on the area or the Confirm button halves the MOV of them all, rounded down, until the end of each one's next turn. Line of Sight is the unit's LoS counted in spaces, and a Wall tile or a wall of the scene between the two blocks it; an enemy in a Thicket is only seen from next to it. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Imbecile.note: The Effect is worded as the players see it: its "allies" are the players' units, the enemies of the unit that has this skill. Those of them within 3 spaces lose the Accuracy and the Dodge.

Embolden.note: The Effect is worded as the players see it: its "enemies" are the units of the side that has this skill. The allies of its unit within 3 spaces gain the Dodge and the Critical Avoid; the unit itself does not.

Discord.note: The Effect is worded as the players see it: its "allies" are the players' units, the enemies of the unit that has this skill. Those of them within 3 spaces lose the Critical and the Critical Avoid.

Calm.note: The Effect is worded as the players see it: its "enemies" are the units of the side that has this skill. The allies of its unit within 3 spaces gain the Accuracy and the Critical; the unit itself does not.

Swiftfoot.note: Every kind of terrain the unit can cross takes it 1 movement a space. It crosses Mountain and Peak; Cliff and Water still ask for a skill of their own.

Spectral Form.note: As for a Flying unit: every space takes 1 movement, Mountain, Cliff and Water included, the tile it stands on gives no DEF, RES or Dodge, and a tile that heals still heals. A Wall stops it as it stops a Flying unit.

Phasing.note: An impassable obstacle is any tile the unit cannot cross: a Wall, and terrain that asks for a skill it does not have (Mountain, Peak, Cliff, Water). Each takes 2 movement to pass through, and the unit cannot end its movement on one. Units in the way are no obstacles.

Bypass.note: The enemy moved through is the one on the way from where the unit's turn began to the tile it stands on or attacks from, and the forecast counts it before the unit moves. With Nimble the first enemy takes no movement but what the terrain under it adds: none on a Plain, 1 in a Forest.

Flyby.note: A tile holds two units at most, one of them with Flyby: the unit walks onto another unit when that unit is clicked (an enemy with Alt held, since a plain click attacks it), and any unit may walk onto its tile the same way. To attack from the enemy's own tile, click that enemy a second time in the forecast. Two units in one space fight as from the next tile. While it shares a tile the unit is in no enemy's way; the unit it shares with still is.

Canto.note: After the unit attacks, the map gives it its range back for the movement it has not spent: it moves again, or Waits. A Gambit counts as attacking.

Tackle.note: Once a fight its unit started is over, the tile its target would be shoved to lights up on the map: a click on it Shoves the target as the Shove command would, 2 spaces with Smite switched on, and a click anywhere else passes. It is offered while the target stands next to the unit and can be shoved, and is no Action of its own.

Action Surge.note: The second Action follows the first, whatever it was but Waiting. It brings no movement of its own: the unit moves with what it has not spent.

Greenhorn.note: Bonus EXP is given with the Give button beside EXP on the sheet, and is not doubled.

Guidance.note: "1.5x extra EXP" is read as 1.5 times the experience.

Loot.note: An enemy brought to 0 HP by hand counts as defeated by the unit selected on the map.

Payment.note: A promotion that takes the place of a level up pays for each stat the new class raises. Stats a class gives on reaching a level pay as increases of their own, after the growth rates rolled at that level.

Revitalize.note: A promotion that takes the place of a level up counts, with the stats the new class raises as the stats levelled up; so do stats a class gives on reaching a level. Charm and Intelligence are boosted like any other stat.

Aptitude.note: The three growth rates are picked as the skill is learnt. Once all three are picked a player cannot change them; the Game Master still can, on the skill's sheet.

Perfect Shot.note: A ranged attack is one with a weapon that itself reaches 2 tiles or more. A unit that did not move in its turn also answers from 1 tile further until its next turn starts.

Telekinesis.note: The penalties apply when the unit attacks from further than its weapon itself reaches; within the weapon's own Range it attacks as usual.

Longarm.note: Switch the skill on to attack as Longarm does: from next to the foe as a Midrange attack, from 2 tiles with a weapon that does not reach that far itself. From 2 tiles the attack is only offered, and only made, where nothing stands between the two: no other unit, no tile that nothing crosses and no wall; between two tiles that touch at a corner, only where both tiles beside that corner are taken. A forecast of an attack that is in the way says "Something stands in the way".

Reach.note: With tokens on a square grid, an attack on a diagonal neighbour with a melee weapon that reaches 1 tile starts at a distance of 1, where the foe answers as usual; without tokens, type 1 as the distance.

Staff Fighter.note: Only a unit with this skill starts a fight with a staff in its hand, and then against a unit next to it; any other is refused, on the map and from its sheet, unless the staff says otherwise (a Broken Staff). Anybody answers an attack with a staff.

Proficient.note: With the Weapon Level module the unit wields weapons up to 5 WLV above its own, in the types it has a rank in.

Aspected.note: Damage typed in by hand is of the type of the weapon held by the unit selected on the map.

Practiced.note: The rank rises in the proficiency the Character Creator has the unit start with. A unit made without the Creator picks that proficiency, among those it has a rank in, as the skill is put on it.

Knightly Tactics.note: The effect is multiplied by the class tier and then rounded down: +1.5 RES is +1, +3 and +4 at Tiers 1, 2 and 3.

options.hint: +2 MAG, DEX% to Rattle after combat (DEX×1.5% at Tier 2, DEX×2% at Tier 3)

Imperial Tactics.note: The effect is multiplied by the class tier and then rounded down: +1.75 is +1, +3 and +5 at Tiers 1, 2 and 3. Todesrose's chance to Rattle grows as its list says, not by the tier again.

Preparedness.note: When an enemy attacks the unit, whoever acts for it is offered the other weapons in its pack that it may wield, above the dock on their own map, before the fight is rolled: one click changes weapon, Pass or no answer in 20 seconds keeps the one in hand. Nothing is offered to a unit with no other weapon, nor against a foe with Nihil.

Arsonist.note: The Burn this unit inflicts deals 5% of maximum HP more for as many turns as it then has. By hand, the unit that inflicts a condition is the one selected on the map as it is added.

Immunity.note: A change that an enemy's skill would leave on it is refused.

Blood for Blood.note: A condition added by hand is handed back to the unit selected on the map as it is added, if that is an enemy.

Stagger.note: The enemy takes 50% more damage of every kind while it is Stunned, and no longer once the Stun is cured. By hand, the unit that inflicts a condition is the one selected on the map as it is added.

Reverb.note: A burst is rolled for a hit of an attack, also one typed in by hand with the attacker selected on the map. By hand, the unit that inflicts a condition is the one selected on the map as it is added.

Dark Calling.note: Every condition its unit inflicts, with an attack, a staff or a skill, is passed on to the enemies of the unit that stand next to the unit afflicted, for half the turns it was inflicted for, rounded down, and 1 at the least. What is passed on is no condition the unit inflicted: it sets off nothing further, neither Curse Siphon nor another spread.

Toxify.note: The unit is given Poison as a battle begins and as its turn starts, and it never runs out. A unit next to it is given Poison as its own turn starts and as it ends.

Balm.note: Each ally a staff is used on gains the buff: the one it is used on, or every ally a staff for several units reaches. For a second Balm, add the skill again and pick another variant.

Live to Serve.note: With a staff that heals one ally the unit regains what that ally regained. With a staff for several units it regains its share once: as much as the ally that regained the most. A unit a skill has its own staves target regains nothing on top of what the staff heals it for.

Reciprocity.note: The ally that heals this unit with a staff regains what this unit regained. With a staff for several units that ally regains its share once, however many of the units healed have this skill: as much as the one of them that regained the most.

Selfstaff.note: A staff for one ally is used on the unit itself when the unit is picked for it (on the map, a click on the unit; from the sheet, with nobody targeted), whatever the staff does: healing, healing over turns, curing, a buff, a repair. A staff for every ally in reach is for the unit too. Not a staff that moves a unit, gives another go or is used against an enemy; Balmwood heals it once.

Ambulance.note: The +5 HP count for each unit a staff heals, at once or over the turns that follow.

Maim & Mend.note: For its next turn the unit heals allies for half as much again with staves, those for several units and those that heal over the turns that follow too, and with items used on an ally.

Venerable.note: With a staff for several units the DEF and RES are a fifth of the most HP any one ally regained, since they do not stack.

Requiescat.note: Whenever the unit restores HP to an ally, with a staff (each ally a staff for several units heals), an item or a skill, the enemy nearest to that ally within 2 spaces takes half the HP restored, rounded down, as damage of a skill. Where several enemies stand equally near, whoever acts for the unit picks one with a click on the map; with no answer it is the first of them. HP a staff restores over later turns is not counted.

Staffsong.note: The staff does what it does, and the ally it was used on moves and acts again if it had acted, as by any Refresh. A staff that misses Refreshes nobody.

Powerstaff.note: A staff that misses has been used all the same.

Re-Move.note: Rolled once after each Action the unit takes but Waiting, until it comes: once a turn. Where the world plays with Movement Stars, their chance is added to this roll in place of being rolled by itself.

Blessing.note: On a battle map the doubled Range is the reach the map shows for the unit's staves, and a staff is refused beyond it.

Staff Savant.note: The unit's staves lose no use, and reach 10 spaces at the least on a battle map, where a staff is refused beyond its reach. A staff for the units next to its user stays one for those.

option.label: Power Chord
option.hint: Buffs by range and nothing else. 1: +3 STR, MAG, DEF, RES. 2: +5 DEX, LUK, +3 SPD, +2 CON. 3 or more: +3 DEF, RES, +2 MOV.

option.label: Power Chord with songs
option.hint: The same buffs by range, on top of what the unit's other skills lay over its Refresh.

Power Chord.note: The Refresh command first asks how it is used: the regular way, Power Chord alone (cooldown 3), or Power Chord with what the unit's other skills lay over its Refresh (cooldown 5). The ally acts again either way. While the cooldown runs neither is offered. The buffs last until the ally's next turn starts, as Inspiring Song's do; SKL is DEX.

Favored.note: A lethal blow is damage of any kind that would bring the unit to 0 HP. Its use comes back with a new encounter, or on the skill's sheet.

Guardian.note: When an attack the system rolls would bring an ally to 0 HP, and a tile next to that ally lies within the unit's whole movement from where it stands, whoever acts for the unit is offered the save on the map: a click on the ally, or on the tile to come to, takes it, and no click within 30 seconds passes. The ally is then left with 1 HP by that attack, which ends the fight; the unit slides to the tile and picks the ally up whatever it weighs, and the use is spent. An ally too heavy for it to Rescue is set down on a free tile next to it, picked by a die, as the unit's next turn starts. It needs free hands and a unit that can move and act, and does not answer damage that is no attack, nor a Gambit. Passing costs nothing.

Aid.note: The 6 Weight count wherever the unit would carry another: for Rescue, for Take and for being Given a unit, and for the Weight an attempt to capture asks for. They count for nothing else, Shove included.

Courteous.note: Whoever carries the unit, by Rescue, Take or Give, keeps its DEX and SPD as they are for as long as it does. Its Weight still has to be carried: the skill lifts the penalty, not the Weight test.

Savior.note: Carrying an ally or a captive does not halve the unit's DEX and SPD, and an attempt to capture is fought with its stats as they are.

Wings of Hope.note: The ally the unit carries regains 15% of its maximum HP, rounded down and 1 at least, as each of that ally's own turns starts, before its conditions deal their damage; an ally at 0 HP regains nothing. It counts however the unit came to carry the ally: Rescued, Taken or Given.

Miraculous Save.note: The ally the unit sets down with Drop carries the protection until its own next turn starts, which for a unit of the players is the next Player Phase: damage of any kind that would bring it to 0 HP is halved, rounded down, and may be fatal still. An ally that is handed on with Give, or set down because its carrier fell, gains nothing.

Goddess's Blessing.note: A weapon is considered Blessed when its name or its Effect says so (the Blessed weapons and the tome Blessing): write "Blessed" into the Effect of any other weapon the table considers so. Non-Beorc attacks are those made with Laguz, Manakete and Taguel weapons. Damage of any other kind is not taken: conditions, skills, its own weapon backfiring, and a number typed in by hand unless a unit with such a weapon is selected on the map.

Mantle.note: A weapon is considered Blessed when its name or its Effect says so (the Blessed weapons and the tome Blessing): write "Blessed" into the Effect of any other weapon the table considers so. Non-Beorc attacks are those made with Laguz, Manakete and Taguel weapons. Damage of any other kind is not taken: conditions, skills, its own weapon backfiring, and a number typed in by hand unless a unit with such a weapon is selected on the map. Like Nihil it stops what a foe's skills that are chosen when to activate do in the fight.

Canto+.note: Given by itself to Mounted, Flying and Ballistician units. The move follows every Action of its list that the system has as one: attacking, a Gambit, using an item or a staff, a skill used as an Action other than Hold or Bastion, and picking up a captive (rescuing). Each of the others joins as it is built.

Rampart.note: Waiting is the Wait button. Given by itself to a unit with the Armored Special Quality. The allies' chance is rolled for a hit of an attack, also one typed in by hand with the attacker selected on the map; other damage is counted against no defence.

Rouse.note: Used with its button as the unit's turn starts. Given by itself to a unit with the Beast Special Quality. ATK is damage; HST counts as Attack Speed for the unit's own follow-up attack, and END is taken off every hit.

Greed.note: With Plunder on the unit as well this rolls nothing, and Plunder pays 100 Gold for each level. Given by itself to a unit with the Bandit Special Quality.

Gregarious.note: Given by itself to a unit with the Laguz Special Quality. As its turn starts next to an allied unit with that quality, both may Shift whatever their Shift Gauge holds until this unit's next turn starts: whoever acts for each is asked above the dock once a turn, and a unit no player owns Shifts by itself. A Shift made that way ends as that turn starts, unless the gauge then holds enough to Shift or the two still stand side by side; the gauge runs as usual meanwhile, and reverts the unit at 0.

General.note: No enemy moves a unit with General, holds it in place or slows it: it is not offered to an enemy's Shove, swap, staff or grapple, stays where it is when units around it are pushed, loses no MOV to what an enemy puts on it, is not stopped beside an enemy that stops those who pass, and moves again after its Action as if no enemy curbed that. Its allies move it as they would any unit. Lethality and Bane: no attack kills it outright (Lethality, Shatterheart's kill at 1 HP), and nothing cuts its HP by a share (Mangle, Shatterheart); such an attack deals its damage and no more.

Roar of the Crowd.note: The Special Qualities added count for Rampart's buffs only. Allies are read from the tokens on the map.

Feral Instincts.note: Switched on, the Shift button works whatever the Shift Gauge holds, and a Shift gives 25% to stats, -1 MOV and half the experience the system awards; switch it off to Shift the usual way. The gauge still runs as usual: at 0 the unit reverts, and may Shift again at once.

Aggression.note: The Attack button works in humanoid form, with Fists and nothing else: they are put in its hands whenever it reverts and as a map starts, and a unit that carries none is handed them. Such a fight gives half of what a fight in humanoid form usually gives the Shift Gauge, rounded down.

Primal Tenacity.note: A new encounter leaves the Shift Gauge where it was and puts the unit in humanoid form. The Reset button of the sheet still sets the starting gauge.

Demiform.note: Used with its button as the unit's turn starts; it ends when its next turn starts. Bonus EXP is not halved.

Draconic Fury.note: Counted for critical hits in fights the system rolls, for a unit with a Shift Gauge.

Formshift.note: The Shift button works whatever the Shift Gauge holds, and a stone never runs out of transformations. At 0 the gauge still reverts the unit, which may Shift again at once.

Primal Blast.note: As the unit transforms for a fight, before the first attack, every enemy next to it takes a quarter, rounded down, of the stat its stone adds to its Might: STR, or MAG with a stone that says MAG not STR. The unit it fights is caught too where it stands next to it. It can defeat them.

Infection.note: When its unit kills an enemy, by a fight or by anything else, that enemy stands up on the tile it fell on as a Revenant on the unit's side, in the hands of whoever acts for the unit: its HP, STR, MAG, DEF, RES, DEX, SPD and LUK halved, rounded down, with the MOV, CON, LoS and Special Qualities of the Revenant class, at 1 HP, with no skills and nothing but the basic Claws of the Weapons tab. Only an enemy that died is raised: not one that is merely down, that left with a life to spare or that was captured. The Revenant is gone as the battle ends; the unit it was raised from stays as it fell, with what it carried.

Summon.note: Used as an action: the free tiles next to its unit light up, and a click puts the unit's Phantom on one, at full HP, on its summoner's side and in its summoner's player's hands.
