The first time, its weapon type (Sword, Lance or Axe) is picked from a short list and the Phantom is made as a unit of its own, which is kept from then on and comes back each time; its 200 growth points are then assigned in a dialog that opens for whoever summoned it, with none for HP, DEF or RES, and opens again at each summoning until they are assigned. Each time it appears it is handed one weapon of its type, drawn for its level from the list of the Phantom class, which it wields whatever its rank and which is never traded, stolen, stored or sold. One Phantom may be out at a time, more with Multi-Phantom, and the skill says so when one more is asked for. The Phantom keeps to its summoner's level (the level ups it is behind wait on its sheet), gains +2 CON and +1 MOV once as it reaches level 21, and its fights earn its summoner the EXP. It leaves the map as the battle ends, or as it falls; the unit itself stays among the Actors. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Imitate.note: Picked from the unit's menu on the map and used on an ally next to it, as its Action. Until it reverts the unit has that ally's maximum HP, stats with their boosts and caps, Charm and Intelligence, class (with its movement, Weight and what it promotes into), weapon ranks, Special Qualities, skills (each ready and switched off) and flat adjustments to combat stats, as they are on the ally's sheet, and its token takes the ally's look. Its HP, level, experience, growth rates, pack, Gold, supports, Affinity, Wounds, conditions, lasting changes and its skills that speak of Imitate stay its own; its other skills are set aside meanwhile. HP above the ally's maximum are set aside and return when it reverts. A weapon in hand that the ally's ranks do not wield is put away for the first it can wield, and what it held is in hand again afterwards; weapon experience earned meanwhile goes to its own proficiency of that kind. It does not level up, promote or change class until it reverts. A unit of a Laguz, Manakete or Taguel class, one that changes form, or one with the Laguz Special Quality cannot be copied; a copied Refresh gives no Refresh command. It reverts as its fifth turn start from then comes, with the Revert button on its chip or by picking the skill again (no Action), when the battle ends and when a new one begins; the 2 turns it cannot be used start then. Nothing of the unit's own is written over, so it reverts exactly, whatever became of the ally.

Greater Imitate.note: Imitate lasts until the unit's sixth turn start. The stats are STR, MAG, DEX, SPD, LUK, DEF and RES, on top of the ally's, for as long as it imitates.

Lasting Imitate.note: As it reverts, each of STR, MAG, DEX, SPD, LUK, DEF and RES that stood higher while it imitated keeps half of the difference, rounded down, until the unit's next turn starts. What Greater Imitate and the ally's skills added counts as gained.

Imitiation Defense.note: While the unit imitates an ally that has a Special Quality, a weapon that is effective against it multiplies its Might by 1.5 in place of 3 (or of 2 for Earth magic), rounded down. Might a skill or a Combat Art adds to an effective attack is multiplied the same way.

Rise.note: When its unit kills an enemy, by a fight or by anything else, whoever acts for it is asked above the dock whether to raise it (15 seconds; no answer is a no; a unit no player owns always does). The enemy then stands up on the tile it fell on as a unit of its own on the unit's side, with all it had, 1 HP and the Terror quality added, and takes its turns with that side under the Game Master's hand. Nothing is traded with it, stolen from it or sold, and it is at a Weapon Triangle disadvantage against Light tomes, as Reanimate says of undead. Up to 3 are raised per map; a use is counted only when one is. Only an enemy that died is raised: not one that is merely down, that left with a life to spare or that was captured. It is gone as the battle ends; the enemy it was raised from stays as it fell.

Wildkin.note: Used once a map from the Skill list, in any turn of its unit and without taking its Action: a Bear, an Eagle or a Wolf is picked from a short list, the free tiles next to the unit light up, and a click puts the animal on one, on the unit's side and in its player's hands. Its HP, STR, MAG, DEF, RES, DEX, SPD and LUK are the shares of the unit's that the table under this skill lists, as they stand when it is made, rounded down; its MOV, LoS and Special Quality are the table's; the WT column is read as a multiple of the unit's Weight (3, 0.7 and 1.8). The Bear fights with a Tiger Fang, the Eagle with a Talon and the Wolf with a Claw, each of the rank of the unit's best proficiency (E at least), which it wields as a Laguz does. The animal earns no EXP, and is gone as the battle ends.

Spirit Call.note: Used as an action once a map: the Magic type is picked from a short list (Fire, Thunder, Wind, Light or Dark), the free tiles next to its unit light up, and a click puts a Spirit on one, on the unit's side and in its player's hands. The Spirit has the unit's stats as they stand when it is made, 30 HP, and half the unit's DEF and RES, rounded down. It has no skills, and wields the tome of its type (Rexflame, Rexbolt, Rexwind, Rexaura or Balberith) whatever its rank. The sheet has no tome named Rexwind: the Wind Spirit is handed Rexcalibur, the Rex- tome of Wind with a Range of 1-2 like the other four. The Spirit earns no EXP, and is gone as the battle ends. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Conjure.note: Used as an action by the Game Master: a list opens of the units the Game Master has prepared (unit Actors no player owns, by their folders), where each that appears is given a number, 1 to 5 in all; the free tiles next to the unit then light up, and a click puts the first on one and the others on the free tiles nearest to it. They appear as tokens of those units, each with the Terror quality added if it lacks it, on the unit's side and already in the turn order. No Actor is made for them. The cooldown of 3 turns starts as they appear. They are gone as the battle ends. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Disarm.note: Rolled for each attack; if that attack lands and the foe still stands, the foe puts down the weapon in its hand and its Shield. For the rest of that fight it makes no further attack and blocks nothing, and its numbers stay as they were. Afterwards both are in its pack, not equipped, until it takes them up again, which costs it nothing in its own turn. Accessories are worn while they are carried and are not put down. A foe that fights unarmed or with a Non-Beorc weapon (a Laguz, Manakete, Taguel or monster weapon) is not rolled for.

Executioner's Mindset.note: The +2 STR and DEX count from the start of that fight, whose forecast shows them, and last until the end of the unit's next turn. A later fight of that kind sets them anew, not higher.

Ruin.note: The Critical Avoid is lost as the attack lands and deals damage, and counts from the next attack of that fight, whichever unit makes it. Activated again, it is set anew by that hit, not added up.

Jolly Cooperation.note: Applies to units with tokens on the scene. A unit that has Sunlight as well rolls for both, and heals for one of them.

Black Magic.note: The D6 is read from a d100, a sixth of it for each condition.

Cudgel.note: A fifth of the HP the foe has is added to the damage of that attack. The stat is picked by a die as the attack lands, and counts from the next attack of that fight; who follows up stays as the fight began.

Metal Medicine.note: Rolled once each time a staff that heals is used on an ally that is hurt. With a staff for several units one roll counts for all of them: each ally healed regains the HP on top and gains the DEF.

Flense.note: The DEF is lost as the attack lands and deals damage, and counts from the next attack of that fight. For 1 turn is until the end of the foe's next turn. Activated again, it is set anew by that hit, not added up.

Inferno.note: Rolled once as the unit starts a fight with a Fire tome in hand. The target and every enemy next to it are Burned at once, and each takes half the unit's MAG, rounded down, as its own next turn starts: damage of the skill, whatever its defence, which can defeat it and is then the unit's kill.

Fearsome.note: Rolled as the turn of each enemy next to this unit starts, with this unit's chance; that enemy is then Stunned by this unit. A unit that is neither its ally nor its enemy is passed over, and so is an enemy that cannot be targeted.

Dragon Ward.note: Rolled for a hit of an attack on an ally, also one typed in by hand with the attacker selected on the map.

Anathema.note: Damage adds the lowest of the four stats to the weapon's Might in place of the stat the weapon adds; what resists the weapon stays as it is. It is laid on the target as the attack lands, and counts from the target's next attack in that fight.

Prevail.note: Allies within 3 spaces heal other units for twice as much by any means (a staff, an item, a skill, a Refresh that heals), and the bonuses to stats and combat stats in the changes that last which they give, to others or to themselves, are doubled as they are given. Auras, supports and terrain are no buffs a unit does, and what a change takes off is left as it is. The unit itself gains nothing from its own skill.

Medusa's Gaze.note: Eye weapons are the weapons with Eye in their name.

Nimble.note: Enemies are in the unit's way no more than its allies are; it still ends its move on a free tile. An enemy with Obstruct stops it all the same.

Barge.note: Each enemy crossed takes 2 movement on top of the tile's own and loses 10% of its maximum HP, and 5% more for every full 15 in the higher of two ability checks: Warfare, and Animal Handling for a unit with the Mounted quality or Athletics for one without it. Shares of a point are dropped, the damage can defeat, and a move that deals it is not taken back.

Trample.note: Switched on before the unit moves. Every enemy next to a tile the unit moves onto, or on one, takes 4 once, and the unit 2 for each enemy that lost HP; nobody goes below 1 HP. The numbers show over the units before the move is made, and a move that deals damage is not taken back.

Obstruct.note: An enemy that enters a tile next to the unit ends its movement there, whatever lets it move through units; one that starts its turn next to the unit may leave. A unit that is down stops nobody.

Dash.note: Switched on to take effect. A diagonal step is one space and takes what the tile entered takes; it is not taken between two tiles the unit could not enter. Level 6, 11 and 16 are counted from the unit's last promotion (levels 26, 31 and 36 for a Hero), for 4 diagonal steps a move at most.

Canto++.note: While a unit moves again after its Action it keeps the weapon it holds, unless it has this skill. Items are handed over between sheets as at any other time: the system has no Trade command to hold back.

Footwork.note: Every Action but an attack or a Gambit, and not Waiting, which ends the turn.

Constraint.note: Counts for every move an enemy makes after its Action, whichever skill grants it (Canto, Canto+, Footwork, Hit and Run). The movement left is halved once, rounded down, however many units with Constraint are near; an enemy left with none makes no such move.

Shove.note: Every unit has Shove as a command on the battle map, beside Attack and Wait: the units next to it that it may shove light up, and a click on one slides it a space straight on. It may shove a unit, friend or foe, whose Weight is not 3 or more above its own, onto a tile that unit could stand on with nobody there; a wall, the edge of the map, or a unit that is not moved by others stops it. Shoving is the unit's Action. Off a battle map nothing is judged.

Rescue.note: Every unit has Rescue as a command on the battle map, beside Shove and Wait: the allies next to it that it may pick up light up, and a click on one takes that ally off its tile to ride on the unit, shown as a small portrait on its token. It may pick up an ally whose Weight is no more than its own; a Ballistician, a unit that is itself carrying one, and a unit that is not moved by others are not picked up. While it carries an ally its DEX and SPD are halved, and the ally holds no tile, is nobody's target, gives and receives nothing and does nothing; time passes for it all the same. Rescuing is the unit's Action, and ends the turn of the ally picked up. With an ally on board the command reads Drop: a click on a free tile next to the unit that the ally can stand on sets it down there, which is the unit's Action, and a click on an ally next to it that could carry the passenger Gives it away, which is free but leaves the unit no further movement. A unit with free hands Takes the passenger of an ally next to it in the same way, with a click on that ally. A carrier that is Incapacitated sets its passenger down on a free tile next to it, picked by a die; one that dies, retreats or is captured leaves it on its own tile, or on the nearest tile it can stand on. Off a battle map nothing is judged.

Steal.note: Steal is a command of the battle map for a unit that has it, beside Shove and Rescue: a skill gives it (Thievery), and so does a Thief Glove it has equipped. The enemies next to the unit that it may steal from light up, and a click on one lists that enemy's pack above the dock; a click on a weapon or an item takes it into the unit's own pack. The unit's SPD must be higher than the enemy's. What the enemy has in hand stays with it (the weapon it holds, the Shield it has equipped), and so does what it wears (an accessory or a Storage item, which the system has no way to put away); a weapon whose Weight is more than the unit's STR is too heavy, and a weapon a unit was summoned with never changes hands. Each of those is greyed in the list, with the reason on hover, and an enemy the unit may not steal from says why when it is clicked. Stealing is the unit's Action. The rules give a pack no size, so what is taken always goes into the pack. Off a battle map nothing is judged.

Thievery.note: Its unit has the Steal command (see Steal). On a battle map the Open command of the dock lights up the doors and chests it can reach: a door from next to it, a chest from its tile or from next to it. It opens either without a key, as its Action; a chest gives it what the Game Master put in it. A trap or a mine that its unit walks onto or ends its turn on is disarmed, whether a skill laid it (Spell Trap), a unit laid it with an item of the Items tab or the Game Master set it down: it is gone, the unit is neither hurt nor halted and walks on, and its skill's name is shown over it. A unit that flies passes over a Mine or a Trap of the Items tab without touching it, and disarms it by ending its turn on it.

Smite.note: Switched on, the unit's Shove pushes 2 spaces: as far as the way is free, and 1 where the second space is not. What Shoves by a skill, as Tackle does, goes by it too. Switched off it Shoves 1 space.

Bulldozer.note: Shoving an enemy takes 1 movement in place of the unit's Action, while it has 1 left: what it has moved so far then stands, and it goes on moving and acts from where it stands. With no movement left the Shove is its Action. An enemy it shoves, by the command or by a skill such as Tackle, cannot move until the end of its own next turn.

Impact.note: Switched on, an attack that lands in a fight its unit started pushes every other unit next to the target, friend or foe, a space straight away from it once the fight is over, and once however many attacks landed. A unit that is not moved by others, or has nowhere to go, stays.

Lunge.note: Switched on, the unit may start a fight from 2 spaces with a weapon that only reaches 1, where it could step into the space between the two: on a tile it could stand on, with nobody there. In such a fight it has +10 Critical, and once it is over the unit steps into that space, which is not movement of its own. Next to its foe it attacks as usual.

Refresh.note: A command of the unit on the map: the allies it may be used on turn green, and a click has one move and act again. Such an ally is a unit of its side, or of an allied side that has the Phase, which stands next to the unit, has taken its Action this Phase, has no Refresh of its own and is not kept from being Refreshed, as by Hustle. It is the unit's Action, earns what the skill table gives for Refresh, and Canto+ follows it. Off a battle map it is not judged.

Inspiring Song.note: The buffs are picked as the skill is learnt, each once, for 4 points in all. They are laid over every ally the unit Refreshes, by its own Refresh or by a skill that hands one out, and last until that ally's next turn starts. SKL is DEX.

Cantrip.note: The debuffs are picked as the skill is learnt, each once, for 4 points in all. They are put on the enemy nearest to the unit, within 4 spaces, as it Refreshes an ally, and last until the end of that enemy's next turn. Where several enemies stand equally near, the unit's owner clicks one of them on the map, and a die picks if they do not. SKL is DEX.

Hymn.note: Spaces are counted along rows and columns. An ally 3 spaces away is shown in violet: it acts again, but gains nothing from Inspiring Song.

Resonance.note: The allies are clicked one after the other; clicking one a second time, or the Sing button, uses the Refresh on those picked so far. They need only be within the reach the unit's Refresh has, which is next to it unless a skill says otherwise.

Reverberate.note: A click on any ally the Refresh may be used on uses it on all of them.

option.label: Ancient Verse: Heal
option.hint: The ally regains HP equal to this unit's MAG.

option.label: Ancient Verse: Guard
option.hint: The ally gains DEF and RES equal to a quarter of this unit's LUK until its next turn starts.

option.label: Ancient Verse: Calm
option.hint: The ally cannot be critically hit until the end of its next Action.

Ancient Verse.note: The Refresh command first asks how it is used: the regular way, or one of these. Used one of these ways the ally is not given its Action back, so any ally in reach that it does something for may be picked, whether or not it has acted; what the unit's other skills lay over a Refresh still comes with it. DEF and RES last until the ally's next turn starts; a quarter of LUK is rounded down.

option.label: Galdr: Cure
option.hint: The ally is cured of every condition.

option.label: Galdr: Shift
option.hint: The ally's Shift Gauge fills as in one turn in humanoid form.

option.label: Galdr: Stride
option.hint: The ally gains 2 MOV until the end of the turn.

option.label: Galdr: Strength
option.hint: The ally gains STR equal to a quarter of this unit's LUK until the end of the turn.

option.label: Galdr: Magic
option.hint: The ally gains MAG equal to a quarter of this unit's LUK until the end of the turn.

Galdr.note: The Refresh command first asks how it is used: the regular way, or one of these. Used one of these ways the ally is not given its Action back, so any ally in reach that it does something for may be picked, whether or not it has acted. The end of the turn is the end of the Phase that is running. The Shift Gauge changes by what a turn in humanoid form changes it by for that ally, and only an ally with a Shift Gauge is offered for it. STR or MAG is the singer's pick: each is a way of its own.

Call to Arms.note: Every ally the unit Refreshes, as by Lead by Example, has 10 temporary HP until the Phase that is running ends: they count on top of its own HP, over its maximum if need be, and are lost first. When Lead by Example Refreshes the allies around the unit, the unit's owner picks from a short list whether the unit itself acts once more where it stands or moves once more; passing takes the Action.

Offensive Stafftics.note: Read with Staffsong: a staff whose Range is 1-MAG/2 (Physic, Catharsis, Aid) Refreshes the ally it is used on, at any distance it reaches. A staff used against an enemy that hits it lets the unit's owner pick, on the map, one ally within that staff's reach to Refresh, or pass. The ally must have acted, as for any Refresh.

Resilience.note: A hit that is blocked is dealt as if the unit went without the +2 DEF (or RES); every other hit counts it. A Shield that has broken is put away, and the bonus goes with it.

Weapon Guard.note: Switched on and off from the skill list at no cost. Guard, beside it, is the unit's Action: until its next turn starts it blocks at +20 whether or not the skill is switched on, and makes no counter-attack. A weapon blocks physical attacks and a tome magical ones; a staff blocks nothing. Where the unit also has a Shield that can block the attack, the Shield blocks and the weapon does not.

Blockbreaker.note: The chance is rolled as a Shield blocks one of the unit's attacks: the hit is then dealt whole, the Shield still loses the use the block cost it, and 1d6 more.

Splitting Slice.note: The weapon's Might is the one written on it. A tenth of it, rounded down, comes off the Shield on top of the use a block costs.

Fresh Start.note: The first use of a weapon is the first attack that costs it a use, with a weapon that has lost none; the first use of a Shield is its first block, with a Shield that has lost none. Either starts the cooldown, so only one of them comes in a fight.

Make It Count.note: The last use of a weapon is the attack that costs it its last use; the last use of a Shield is the block that leaves it without any.

Phalanx.note: Rolled as a Shield blocks, not as a weapon does. A Shield that takes a share off takes twice the share, 100% at most; one that takes everything gains nothing.

Corrosion.note: Rolled for each attack; the uses come off if that attack lands, on top of what a block costs the Shield. A weapon or Shield brought to 0 uses breaks, and a weapon that breaks attacks no more in that fight.

Batter.note: The tens place of ATK is a tenth of the unit's Atk with the weapon in hand, rounded down. In a fight it is rolled for each attack and the uses come off if that attack lands. As an action it is picked from the unit's menu on the map: the enemies the weapon in hand could attack light up, a click takes the uses off that enemy's Shield without a roll, and for 2 of its turns it has no Shield equipped and can equip none (the Shield it had is in its hands again afterwards). An enemy without a Shield may be picked too. The cooldown is the action's; the chance in a fight is always there. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Shield Bash.note: The attack is made with the Shield, not the weapon: a physical attack on a foe next to the unit, with 70 Hit and the Shield's Might in place of the weapon's (the unit's own DEX, LUK and STR count as ever; no weapon triangle, no effective damage, nothing of the weapon's Effect). It costs neither the Shield nor the weapon a use, earns no weapon experience, and can be made by a unit whose weapon could not answer. The Might is what the Shield takes off a physical attack from next to the unit, 0 for one that takes a share. One block, one attack; an attack made in answer sets off no other.

Wappenschild.note: The enemy's next attack in this fight is not made, if it had one left. After the fight the enemy makes no counter-attack the next time it is attacked from where it could have answered; that is used up by the first such fight, or gone with the map.

Unerring.note: A tally kept on the unit for the rest of the map: +1 DEF and RES for each block with a Shield, up to +10, and 1 less for each roll to block with a Shield that fails, never below 0. A hit its Shield could not block at all, and a block the foe's skill negated, change nothing. It counts from after the fight in which it changed.

Transpierce.note: For each physical attack that lands and is blocked, lessened by a skill of the target (one that takes effect on that hit, or one that always takes damage off), or left with half its damage or less by the target's DEF and terrain: DEX/4 damage, whatever the target's defence, and -3 DEF until the end of the target's next turn. Where the attack dealt no damage and a block or a skill took something off it: DEX/3 and -6 DEF instead. The debuff is renewed by each such attack, not added up.

Gamble.note: A switch, ticked in the forecast or from the list of skills: while it is on it counts in every fight, also when the unit is attacked. Accuracy is the unit's own, before the weapon triangle and the foe's Dodge; Critical is its own, before the foe's Critical Avoid. Both are rounded down.

Critical Force.note: A switch, ticked in the forecast. "Base Critical" is the unit's Critical before the foe's Critical Avoid. A unit is able to Critical unless a skill or a condition keeps it from critical hits; one whose chance is 0 only because of the foe's Critical Avoid still trades.

Reckless Charge.note: A switch, ticked in the forecast or from the list of skills: while it is on it counts in every fight, also when the unit is attacked. Each trade is made as often as the unit has to give, unless it picked a number in the forecast, which is kept. END is what its supports and skills give it.

Ebb and Flow.note: A switch, ticked in the forecast or from the list of skills: while it is on it counts in every fight, also when the unit is attacked. Each trade is made as often as the unit has to give, unless it picked a number in the forecast, which is kept. ATK is damage; HST is what its supports and skills give it, with what Reckless Charge has just made of its END where that comes first among its skills.

Infuse.note: A switch, ticked in the forecast. The attack stays a physical one for Shields and for what asks for a physical or a magical attack; only what resists it changes.

Magic Weapons.note: A switch, ticked in the forecast. The attack stays a physical one for Shields and for what asks for a physical or a magical attack; only what resists it changes.

Lull.note: A bonus is what the foe's own skills, the auras it receives and the changes that last on it add to a stat (STR, MAG, DEX, SPD, LUK, DEF, RES or CON); what its class, its level, its form, its supports and its tile give it is none. The stat is the one the foe gains the most in, unless the unit picked another in the forecast, which is kept until it picks again.

Incantation.note: Ticked in the forecast, with the number of times 3 HP are spent picked beside it (once unless picked, and kept); or switched on beforehand for a fight in which the unit is attacked and can answer. The HP are paid as the fight begins and the Might lasts for that fight; the unit keeps 1 HP. A unit that makes no attack spends nothing, and the skill stays on.

Extract Power.note: Ticked in the forecast, with the number of transformations given up picked beside it (one unless picked, and kept). They are those a stone still has for the unit this turn once this fight has had its own, and are counted as used when the fight is over; the damage is for every attack of the unit in that fight. A unit that changes form by a Shift Gauge has none to give.

Rend Heaven.note: When it activates, the attack adds half of MAG to the damage of a weapon that adds STR, or half of STR to that of one that adds MAG, and is resisted by whichever of the foe's DEF and RES leaves more damage, with what its tile adds to each.

Parity.note: A switch, ticked in the forecast or from the list of skills; while it is on it counts in every fight, also when the unit is attacked. For both units the fight is then fought without what tiles and height give, without what supports add, without Shields, and without skills, auras and lasting changes, save what a skill that was switched on before the fight does and what comes once the fight is over (on a kill, after combat). Of a weapon's Effect only the stat it adds, what it counts as, that it may backfire and that it is Midrange stay, and the effective damage of bows, crossbows, bolts and Wind. Conditions, Combat Arts, the weapon triangle, Affinity effects and what carrying a unit does are no such effects and stay.

Cauterize.note: A bonus is what the foe's own skills, the auras it receives and the changes that last on it add to SPD and RES; each becomes a penalty of the same size for the fight. The foe's HP are those it has as the fight begins.

Overdrive.note: Every cooldown of the unit's skills that starts while it has this skill is 1 turn shorter; a cooldown of 1 turn leaves the skill ready again on the unit's next turn.

True Strike.note: When an attack roll of the unit misses by 10 or less, or a hit of its fails its critical roll by 10 or less, whoever acts for it is offered to roll again, once in a fight for either. The new roll stands; a roll that an answer of the foe turned into a miss (a guaranteed dodge) is no missed roll.

Manaward.note: When a hit lands on the unit, once what blocks it and what lessens it by itself are counted, whoever acts for the unit is offered each Tome it carries that has 2 uses left, with what its Might would take off; one click spends the 2 uses and lessens the hit, once in a fight. A Tome that never wears out costs nothing. The Tome in hand may be the one spent, and breaks if that was its last use.

Chop Down.note: On a Critical Hit, where another enemy stands next to the unit or next to its foe, whoever acts for the unit is offered to forgo the damage of the critical: the hit then deals its plain damage, and half of the hit's damage before the foe's defence goes to 2 such enemies once the fight is over, picked on the map where there are more than 2. On a hit that fails its critical roll by 10 or less it is offered half of the unit's Atk as damage to the target for 4 uses of the weapon, with more than 4 uses left; that comes once the hit is dealt. Both ignore defence and END, as damage a skill deals does, can defeat, and count as the unit's kill.

Close Call.note: Rolled by itself, LUK% each time: for each skill its foe chose for the fight and for the Combat Art its foe performs, before the fight is planned (one that is negated is spent and does nothing); as an answer of its foe's Choose skill is taken; as a critical hit lands on it (the hit lands without the damage of one); as a skill of its foe rolls to activate and does; and as its foe blocks a hit of its. A chance of the foe that is no skill activation (a Shield's own, a Special Quality's) is not negated.

Cancel.note: Rolled as the fight begins and with each of the unit's attacks, whether or not the attack lands. The foe's next attack in that fight is not made: nothing is rolled for it and it costs nothing. One attack waits to be cancelled at a time, however often the chance comes before it.

Enervation.note: Rolled with each of the unit's attacks, and laid on the target if that attack lands, as every change a skill puts on a foe is. The target then rolls each Hit roll twice and takes the worse, from its next attack in that fight until the end of its next turn (the turn after this one, for a target that is in its own turn).

Diversion.note: Rolled as an enemy starts a fight in which the unit can counter-attack: it then attacks first in every round of that fight, and its foe answers. The fight is still one its foe began, for whatever asks who did.

Accost.note: Rolled as each round of a fight ends in which both units still stand and an attack was made, whoever began it: the same attacks are made again in the same order, with their own dice, up to 20 further rounds. Before each, whoever acts for the unit is offered to end the fight instead, with the HP of both; no answer within 15 seconds fights on. A unit no player owns ends it where the round would defeat it and not its foe.

Bushwhack.note: As each round ends, a unit with more Attack Speed than its foe that then has more HP than it fights the round again, up to 40 further rounds, each with its own dice. Before each, whoever acts for the unit may end the fight instead; a unit no player owns ends it where the round would defeat it and not its foe.

Thunderstorm.note: Rolled as the unit starts a fight. Its follow-up attack is then made right after its first, before its foe's counter-attack; a unit that makes no follow-up makes one more attack there instead. The +15 Hit and Critical and +3 damage count for all its attacks of that fight.

Ravage.note: A unit that would make 2 attacks or more in a fight (a follow-up, or a weapon that strikes twice) makes one more after all others, on either side of a fight. The forecast counts it.

Pursuit.note: In a fight the unit starts, its 2nd attack has +1 Might and +3 Critical, its 3rd +2 and +6, and so on for every attack it makes in that fight, whatever the attack is (each strike of a weapon that strikes twice, a follow-up, an attack a skill adds). The forecast shows what each attack deals.

Strong Riposte.note: In a fight an enemy starts, the unit's 2nd attack has +1 Might and +3 Critical, its 3rd +2 and +6, and so on for every attack it makes in that fight. The forecast shows what each attack deals.

Penetration.note: From its 2nd attack of a fight on, each of the unit's attacks ignores a third of whichever of DEF and RES resists it; what is left of that defence is rounded down. The forecast shows what each attack deals.

Crusader's Ward.note: Rolled once as an enemy starts a fight. For that fight the unit then takes half the damage of every attack after the first that is made against it; against a foe that makes no more than one attack, a quarter less from that one. It comes off the hit after a block and before the unit's other skills.

Guard.note: Every 2nd attack made against the unit deals half its damage. The attacks are counted hit or miss, across fights, from the start of the unit's own turn until its next turn starts; outside of a battle each fight counts by itself. The forecast shows what each attack deals.

Beatdown.note: A weapon that strikes twice "when initiating combat" strikes twice for this unit whoever began the fight. The forecast counts the strikes.

Flèche.note: In a fight the unit starts against a foe it follows up on: +1 damage and +3 Hit and Critical for every 3 Attack Speed it has over that foe beyond the 4 a follow-up takes. HST does not count towards it. The sums behind the forecast's numbers name it.

Staff Mage.note: An Offensive Staff used on one enemy is cast a second time at once where the unit's Attack Speed with the staff, with 3 HST, is 4 or more above the enemy's. A staff that inflicts a condition is only cast again if the first cast missed, and a staff for each enemy in range never is. The second cast rolls its own hit and costs the staff another use.

Revenge.note: Rolled each time an attack lands on the unit and deals damage, at 3% for each point of damage it dealt: a unit that still stands and can attack its foe from there makes one more attack at once, with +15 Hit. An attack made that way sets off no other.

Quickclaw.note: Rolled once as an enemy starts a fight from 2 or 3 spaces. The unit then makes one attack in each round of that fight whose damage before the foe's defence is its STR: a physical attack with the Hit of the weapon in hand, which costs that weapon no use. A unit that cannot answer makes it in place of its counter-attack; one that can makes it right after its first attack.

Handgonne.note: Rolled as an enemy starts a fight from where the unit's weapon does not reach, no further away than the unit's Line of Sight counts spaces: the unit then makes one counter-attack with the weapon in hand, in the place a counter-attack has. Not for a unit that is kept from counter-attacking by something other than its weapon's reach.

Arcane Rush.note: Rolled for each of the unit's attacks with a physical weapon from next to its foe: the attack is followed at once by a second one that adds MAG to the weapon's Might in place of the stat the weapon adds and is resisted by RES. Each of the two costs the weapon a use.

Adaptation.left: Its second half waits for the Dismounting Optional Module, which the system does not have yet: +10 Hit against infantry units while mounted is written and counts as soon as that module is in use, and +10 Hit against Mounted units while dismounted needs the module to say that a unit is dismounted.
Adaptation.note: While its unit is at a Weapon Triangle disadvantage, the triangle changes nobody's Hit in that fight: the unit loses none and its foe gains none. What it does to damage stays, and so does the advantage itself, for whatever asks who has it (Breaking). A mounted unit is one with the Mounted or Flying quality, an infantry unit one with neither.

Assault.note: The unit has Weapon Triangle advantage against every weapon that stands outside the triangle of the weapon it holds: another triangle, or none at all. Swords, Axes and Lances are one triangle and every kind of magic is another; with a weapon that stands in no triangle itself, as a bow does unless the world plays with the extended triangle, every other weapon is outside. Within its own triangle the weapons decide as ever. Both units need a weapon in hand, the bonus goes by the unit's rank with its own, and where both units are handed the advantage the weapons decide.

Deeper Knowledge.note: Rolled for each of the unit's attacks in a fight where the Weapon Triangle counts. For that attack the Hit and damage the triangle gives the unit are counted four times, with whatever already multiplies them, and the Hit and damage it takes off the unit are not taken off. The foe's attacks are as they were.

Trilemma.note: A switch, ticked in the forecast. In a fight its unit starts, the Hit and damage the Weapon Triangle gives and takes are doubled for both units; from then until its unit's next turn starts they are doubled in every fight it is in, also when it is attacked and also once the switch is off again. The skill and the change it leaves count once, so a second fight in the same turn is doubled, not quadrupled; a foe with Trilemma of its own doubles it again.

Symbiosis.note: With a Dark or Light tome in hand the unit is never at a Weapon Triangle disadvantage: where its foe would have the advantage, neither has, so the foe gains nothing either and cannot Break it. A Light tome takes from the Dark tome the unit last attacked with, and a Dark tome from the Light one: half its Might, a quarter of its Hit and half its Critical, each rounded down, for the first attack made with the tome since it was taken in hand, hit or miss. The Might counts as the tome's own. Taking the same tome in hand again counts as a new equip. What the unit last attacked with is remembered from fight to fight, with no end.

Vanquish.note: The lower of DEF and RES is the one that leaves more damage, with what the foe's tile adds to each.

Hellhound.note: Every hit that deals damage is followed by a second blow of Fire damage: half the damage the hit dealt, less the foe's RES and what its tile adds to it, and no less than a quarter of that damage, all rounded down. It is dealt whatever blocks or lessens a hit, can defeat the foe, and counts as the unit's kill. The forecast counts it in the damage and names it behind the number.

Northswain's Glow.note: The average of MAG, RES and LUK is rounded down. Against a foe with the Terror quality the attack deals effective damage, unless it already does.

Show of Force.note: Base damage is the Might written on the weapon and the stat it adds, less the foe's DEF or RES, without tiles, the weapon triangle, supports or skills. Where that is more than the HP the foe has as the fight begins, the weapon's Might counts twice for the whole fight, and an effective weapon multiplies both.

Mangle.note: Rolled as each attack is made. If the attack lands, a D100 is rolled and the hit deals that share of the target's maximum HP, rounded down, in place of its damage, unless its own damage (with a critical hit, if it is one) is as much or more. What blocks or lessens a hit still does. A unit with General takes the attack's own damage, and nothing is rolled.

Shatterheart.note: If the attack lands, the target loses half of the HP it has left once the hit's damage is dealt, rounded down, whether or not the hit dealt any; a target that is left at 1 HP is killed instead. That is a blow of its own: it counts as the unit's kill, and what saves a unit from a lethal blow may save it. A unit with General is spared both.

Lethality.note: Rolled as each attack is made, at half the unit's Critical with the weapon in hand, before the foe's Critical Avoid. If the attack lands it deals at least the HP its target has left, whatever blocked or lessened the hit. Most units are all but those with General. It is a lethal blow like any other: what halves one, saves a unit from one or holds a hit to a share of its HP still does.

Ironhide.note: The rank is the one written on the foe's weapon. A weapon is effective against the unit when its attacks deal effective damage to it, by its Effect or by a skill of its wielder. Half is rounded down.

Unstoppable.note: A weapon that is effective against several of the unit's Special Qualities still is for the others. An Armor-effective weapon is one whose attacks are effective against Armored units, by its Effect or by a skill of its wielder, whatever it then deals to this unit.

Greater Terror.note: A Terror-effective weapon is one whose attacks are effective against Terror units, by its Effect or by a skill of its wielder. Expel is not rolled against the unit: it is left out where the staff picks its targets.

Dark Veil.note: Rolled once as the fight begins, against a foe whose attacks are not effective against Terror units, by its weapon's Effect or by its skills.

Titanomachy.note: Counted from the unit's CON without skills and the Weight written on the weapon in hand, for up to 6 points; nothing without a weapon.

Collector.note: Counts every weapon, tome and staff the unit carries that it may not wield, by its ranks and what its skills add to them. A broken weapon does not count.

Weapon Insight.note: The unit has Proficiency in a weapon type it has a rank with, E or higher; a kind of weapon that has no proficiency, such as a monster's, is never one.

Tenacity.note: The amount of stat debuffs is the points the foe's stats (STR, MAG, DEX, SPD, LUK, DEF, RES, CON) are lowered by in all as the fight begins: by conditions, by changes that last on it, by auras, and by skills of this unit in this fight.

Killing Machine.note: The unit's Critical with the weapon in hand is doubled once everything is added to it, before the foe's Critical Avoid.

Ambush.note: Other enemies are the unit's enemies that stand within 2 spaces of its foe. A foe cannot make Follow-ups when it makes none in this fight, as its Attack Speed and skills stand when the fight begins: for want of Attack Speed, for being kept from them, or for making no counter-attack at all.

Serenity.note: The turn is the turn of the battle the unit is in, as its encounter counts it. Outside of a battle there is no turn: the skill is then shown as one to check by hand, and nothing of it is applied.

Tempest.note: The turn is the turn of the battle the unit is in, as its encounter counts it. Outside of a battle there is no turn: the skill is then shown as one to check by hand, and nothing of it is applied.

Evened Out.note: The turn is the turn of the battle the unit is in, as its encounter counts it. Outside of a battle there is no turn: the skill is then shown as one to check by hand, and nothing of it is applied.

Better Odds.note: The turn is the turn of the battle the unit is in, as its encounter counts it. Outside of a battle there is no turn: the skill is then shown as one to check by hand, and nothing of it is applied.

Quick Burn.note: +15 on the first turn of a battle, +14 on the second, and so on down to nothing from the sixteenth. Outside of a battle no map has begun: the skill is then shown as one to check by hand, and nothing of it is applied.

Channel.note: Magical damage is a hit of an attack made with a tome that deals damage. The first of them each turn, counted from the start of its unit's own turn, is halved by itself (the sheet marks the skill as chosen when to activate, but its Effect leaves nothing to choose), and what was taken off it is added to the damage of its unit's next attack, in that fight or in a later one on the same map; a second bonus takes the place of the first.

Rancor.note: The damage its hits deal is counted from the start of its unit's own turn until its next turn starts, in fights the system rolls, what it deals in the other sides' Phases included. ATK is damage: +1 for every 10 counted, for its unit's next turn, from its start to its end.

Proud Fighter.note: +2 STR for each fight its unit starts, from that fight on, +10 at the most. It is lost at the end of a turn of its unit in which it started no fight.

Bloody Glee.note: Kept for the rest of the map, as its Effect does not say that it lasts between maps. A critical hit that defeats its foe empties the count first, and is then counted as one.

Untouchable.note: Counted in fights the system rolls, from the unit's next attack of that fight on, and kept for the rest of the map. A hit is an attack that lands on it, whatever it deals.

Executioner.note: +1 to each of the six stats for each enemy defeated, by whatever means, ten times at the most. It is over as the battle ends.

Curse Siphon.note: Their HP is maximum HP, rounded down, for each condition its unit inflicts, with an attack, a staff or a skill. An action is the Action of one of its unit's turns: the bonus is lost at the end of the second turn in a row in which it inflicted none.

Criticality.note: Every attack its unit makes in a fight the system rolls that is no critical hit counts, a miss included, from its next attack on; the count is kept from map to map. The 1% holds whatever the foe's Critical Avoid, not against a foe that cannot be critically hit.

First Blood.note: Its one use comes back as a battle begins. The first attack its unit makes is a hit and a critical hit, unless something keeps it from critical hits; an attack that lands on it before that, whatever it deals, uses the skill up instead. Fights outside of a battle count for the map that follows.

Multishot.note: Rolled once as the unit starts a fight with a Bow in hand, where another enemy stands next to the target and not next to the unit. Once the fight is over the unit makes one attack on that enemy with the Bow, at whatever distance it stands, which costs the Bow a use and is not answered. Where several enemies stand so, whoever acts for the unit picks one on the map, and the nearest to the target is taken where they do not.

Collateral.note: Offered each time an attack from 2 spaces or more lands, where an enemy stands in a straight line behind the target, no further behind it than the weapon in hand reaches at the most. Once the fight is over the unit attacks each of them in turn, nearest first: the first at -20 Hit for half its damage, each one after at 10 Hit less and half the damage of the one before. None of these attacks costs the weapon a use, and none is answered.

Whirlwind.note: Rolled for each of the unit's attacks. The additional attack is made right after that attack with Elwind as the Weapons tab has it (Might 5, Hit 80, Critical 5, 1-2 range, effective against Flying, 25% to Squall), DEX added to its Might and resisted by RES; the unit needs no Elwind, and the attack costs nothing. Once the fight is over every enemy next to the unit, its foe included, is pushed a space straight away from it; one that a wall, the edge of the map, another unit or ground it cannot stand on keeps in place takes 5 damage instead.

Phantom Support.note: Given by each Phantom the unit has summoned, from where that Phantom stands, to its allies within 3 spaces that were not summoned themselves, the summoner included, while the summoner stands on the map with the skill equipped. An ally near several Phantoms gains it once, from the nearest.

Bounty Hunter.note: Used from the Skill list once a map, which takes no Action: every enemy on the map lights up and a click selects one. In a fight against it the unit has +2 STR, MAG, DEX, SPD, LUK, DEF, RES and CON and +10 Hit, Dodge and Critical, which the forecast counts. The choice stands for the map, also once that enemy is defeated. Whom the unit attacks is its Game Master's to play: the system does not move enemy units.

Headhunter.note: Used from the Skill list once a map, which takes no Action: every enemy on the map lights up and a click selects one. In a fight against it the unit has +3 STR, MAG, DEX, SPD, LUK, DEF, RES and CON, +10 Hit, Dodge and Critical, and its attacks deal effective damage, which the forecast counts. The choice stands for the map, also once that enemy is defeated. Whom the unit attacks is its Game Master's to play: the system does not move enemy units.

Got Your Back.note: As an enemy confirms an attack on an ally next to its unit, whoever acts for the unit is offered, in one click, to fight in that ally's place: the fight is then the unit's, at the distance to the ally and on the ally's ground, with +3 END, and once it is over the two trade places if both still stand and may be moved. No answer in time is a no, and the enemy's forecast names the unit as one that may step in. A unit no player owns steps in where the attacks would not defeat it and would either defeat the ally or take more off the ally than off itself. A unit that stands guard for the ally (Protect) comes first.

Terrorguard.note: As an enemy confirms an attack on its unit, or on an ally, whoever acts for the unit is offered, in one click, to have an allied Terror unit next to its unit fight in that place: in its own, or in that of an ally which stands next to that Terror as well. The fight is then the Terror's, at the distance and on the ground of the unit it stands in for. Each such Terror is offered in turn; no answer in time is a no. A unit no player owns has the Terror fight where the attacks would not defeat it and would either defeat the unit attacked or take more off that unit than off the Terror. It is about fights an enemy starts: its unit attacks with its own hands.

Aurablast.note: With a melee weapon in hand the unit also attacks from 2 spaces, which the map offers with the rest of its range: from there the fight is fought with the numbers of Arclight as the Weapons tab has it (Might, Hit, Critical, Weight, MAG against RES, Light for the weapon triangle, what it is effective against and its chance to Brighten), and the forecast names Arclight with the skill's mark. The melee weapon is still what is swung: it loses its use on a hit, as its kind does, and earns its own weapon experience. From a distance the weapon in hand reaches by itself it attacks as ever, and counter-attacks are made with the weapon in hand.

Shadowgift.note: With a melee weapon in hand the unit also attacks from 2 spaces, which the map offers with the rest of its range: from there the fight is fought with the numbers of Carreau as the Weapons tab has it (Might, Hit, Critical, Weight, MAG against RES, Dark for the weapon triangle and its chance to Darken), and the forecast names Carreau with the skill's mark. The melee weapon is still what is swung: it loses its use on a hit, as its kind does, and earns its own weapon experience. From a distance the weapon in hand reaches by itself it attacks as ever, and counter-attacks are made with the weapon in hand.

Vortex.note: The Wind tomes of the Weapons tab with a Range of 1-2 whose rank is that of the unit's highest proficiency, in any kind of weapon, are listed with the unit's own weapons in the dock, marked with the skill; where no Wind tome has that rank, those of the next rank below that has one. One that is taken up is what the unit attacks with in the fights it starts, whatever is in its hand and whatever its Wind rank: it has no uses to lose, cannot be traded or put away, and earns Wind weapon experience as the tome does. It is put down again once the unit has attacked with it or acted, and counter-attacks are made with the weapon in hand.

Firebreathing.note: When the unit starts a fight with a Fire tome and an enemy stands on the tile right behind its target, in a straight line from the unit along a row or a column, that tile is painted with the target's in the forecast, with the damage and the Hit of the attack over the enemy there. Once the fight is over the unit attacks that enemy once as well, with the same tome and its full numbers, rolled by itself and shown over it: it costs the tome no further use and is not answered. A unit that fell in the fight makes no such attack.

Draconic Heritage.note: Rolled as the unit starts a fight with Breath Weapon, before anything else: on a success that fight is fought with the Rex- tome of the same type and a Range of 1-2 on the Weapons tab (Rexburst, Rexflame, Rexbolt, Rexcalibur, Rexocean, Rexfrost, Rexboulder) in place of the Arc- tome, with whatever that tome's Effect adds. The forecast shows the Arc- tome, since the roll comes as the attack is confirmed; the card of the fight shows the roll and the tome that was used. A foe with Nihil cancels it.

Pillage.note: Given by itself to a unit with the Bandit Special Quality, as Greed is. A unit that has it and is no friend of the players' side (an enemy, or a unit that stands apart) may Destroy a Village from the Village's tile with the Open command of the dock, as its Action: the Village then gives nothing to anybody. A Village that was visited has shut its gates and is not destroyed. A unit of the players' side or of their allies visits Villages instead, whatever its qualities.

Watchful.note: Steal refuses its unit and says why, a skill that takes an item or gold from a foe in a fight takes nothing from it, and with Capturing an attempt to capture it is refused.

Multi-Phantom.note: Its unit may have one more Phantom out at once, a third from level 26 and a fourth from level 31 (levels 6 and 11 of Tier 2). Each is a unit of its own with its own weapon type and growth rates.

Phantom Skill.note: As the skill is learnt the Compendium opens at the Generic Skills, where one is picked for the unit's Phantoms; it is kept as the skill's choice, which the Game Master can change in Edit mode. Every Phantom the unit summons has that skill equipped from then on, and one that is already out is given it at once. Until one is picked the Compendium opens again each time a Phantom is summoned.

Reanimate.note: Used as an action: a Steel Sword, Lance or Axe is picked from a short list, the free tiles next to its unit light up, and a click puts an undead minion on one. Its HP, STR, MAG, DEF, RES, DEX, SPD and LUK are three quarters of the unit's as they stand when it is made, rounded down, with STR read from the unit's MAG; its MOV, CON and LoS are the unit's. It has the Terror quality, no skills, and the one weapon it came with, which it wields whatever its rank; nothing is traded with it, stolen from it or sold. It is at a Weapon Triangle disadvantage against Light tomes whatever it wields. It is on the unit's side and takes its turns under the Game Master's hand. Three minions made by this skill may stand at once (those Rise raised are not counted), and the skill says so when a fourth is asked for. Minions are gone as the battle ends. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

act.label: Take control of it (+3 to six stats)

instead.label: Have it fight in this unit's place

Possession.note: Used as an action on an undead the unit raised with Rise or made with Reanimate. Within 3 spaces, on one that has yet to act this turn: whoever acts for the unit acts for that undead, with +3 STR, DEF, RES, DEX, SPD and CON, until the undead's turn ends; it then goes back to the Game Master's hand. On one next to the unit, in place of that: the undead fights in the unit's place when an enemy starts a fight with the unit, as Protect has it, until the unit's next turn starts, with a filled shield on its token. Where both are open, which is picked from a short list above the dock.

Divide.note: Used as an action: how many Mogalls are made is picked from a short list (as many as the 5 on the field, the free tiles next to the unit and its HP allow; each costs 5 HP and the unit keeps 1 at least), the free tiles next to its unit light up, and a click puts the first on one and the others on the free tiles nearest to it, no further than 3 spaces from the unit. Each is a unit of the Mogall class on the unit's side, in the hands of whoever acts for the unit: its HP, STR, MAG, DEF, RES, DEX, SPD and LUK a third of the unit's as they stand, rounded down, its MOV, CON, LoS and Special Qualities those of the Mogall class, with the basic Eye of the Weapons tab. No more than 5 Mogalls made by this skill stand on the map at once, whoever made them. They are gone as the battle ends. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Reinforce.note: Used as an action by the Game Master: a list opens of the units the Game Master has prepared (unit Actors no player owns, by their folders), where each that arrives is given a number, up to 12 in all; every free tile of the map then lights up, and a click puts the first on the tile picked and the others on the free tiles nearest to it. They appear as tokens of those units on the unit's side, already in the turn order, and are ordinary units from then on: they stay when the battle ends, and no Actor is made for them. Off a battle map the action is only counted.

Down Not Out.note: Rolled by itself, LUK/2%, whenever its unit would take an Injury: as it gets back up from Incapacitation, whatever healed it. The roll stands on the card that tells of the unit getting back up, where the Injury would have been, and the skill's name is shown over the unit when it spares it. Injuries set by hand on the sheet are not rolled for.

Glance.note: Rolled by itself, LUK%, for each Wound its unit would take: a hit of an attack that deals its maximum HP divided by 1.5 or more, in a fight the system rolls, from a Gambit, from a hit an ally's skill passed on to it, or taken off its HP by hand in Play mode. The roll stands on the fight's card where the Wound would have been (on a short card of its own outside a fight), and the skill's name is shown over the unit when it spares it. Wounds set by hand on the sheet are not rolled for.

Triangle Attack.note: Not asked: whenever its unit starts a fight while the formation stands, its first attack of that fight is the Triangle Attack, which cannot miss and is a critical hit. The formation stands where the unit, from the tile it attacks from, and two allies that have this skill equipped each stand 1 or 2 spaces from the enemy, the three are not in one line, and the enemy's space lies inside the triangle between them, its edges included: three units on three sides of it, as in the games, or two on opposite sides with the third anywhere off their line; three that all stand to one side of it make none. Only the unit attacks: the two allies spend nothing, need no weapon that reaches, and may have acted already. The forecast shows it before the attack is confirmed: the two allies are ringed on the map, a chip names them, and Hit and Crit already read 100. A foe that cancels skills chosen when to activate stops it, as the sheet marks it one.

Delta Attack.note: Not asked: whenever its unit starts a fight while the formation stands, its first attack of that fight is the Delta Attack and deals five times its damage, counted after the foe's defence; it is rolled to hit like any other attack. The formation is the Triangle Attack's: the unit, from the tile it attacks from, and two allies that have this skill equipped each stand 1 or 2 spaces from the enemy, not in one line, with the enemy's space inside the triangle between them, its edges included. Only the unit attacks, and the two allies spend nothing. The forecast shows it before the attack is confirmed: the two allies are ringed on the map, a chip names them, and the damage is already the multiplied one.

Forecast.note: The Game Master switches the weather of a map on and off from the Phase banner, and each kind then does what the Weather page says by itself. Its unit is spared the effects of weather: tiles cost it no more MOV in Rain, a Snowstorm, a Thunderstorm or a Windstorm, it loses no SPD in a Heat Wave, and it takes no damage as its turn ends in Hail or a Heat Wave. It is not spared Fog of War, with the LoS of 4 a Mist gives every unit, nor a bolt of lightning or of ballista fire that strikes its tile. The weather icon of the banner says on hover that the selected unit is spared. Fog of War itself is not drawn by the system and is the Game Master's to run, and the Fatigue of a Heat Wave waits for that Optional Module.

Sapper.note: A unit lays a Mine or a Trap of the Items tab by using the item on a battle map: the free tiles next to it light up, a click lays it there, and that is its Action. It lies hidden from the other side until a unit walks onto it or ends its turn on it; a unit that flies springs it only by ending its turn there, and the unit that laid it never does. What its unit lays has, from the moment it is laid: +5 damage for a Mine that deals damage (an item whose name says Mine or Bomb: the Mine and the Frey Bomb; a Stun Mine deals none to add to), and one turn more for every condition a mine or a trap of its gives (Bear Trap, Silence Trap, Stun Mine, Sleep Trap, Poison Trap). Its unit gains +10 EXP as an enemy springs one of them, and +25 more as the damage of one of its Mines defeats that enemy; a unit that is no enemy of its springs them too, and earns it nothing.

Fast Recovery.note: Whenever an item restores HP to the unit, Used by itself or on it by an ally: half the HP it regained, rounded down, are restored again as its next turn starts, and the card of the item says how many. Two items before that turn heal for both. An item that restored nothing leaves nothing.

Belligerent.note: Asked each time the unit Uses an item that restores HP on itself, before it heals: with a yes the item restores half as much, rounded down, and the unit has +2 STR, MAG, DEF, RES, DEX, SPD, LUK and CON until its next turn starts. "All stats" is read as those seven and CON, not HP, MOV or LoS. An item an ally Uses on the unit does not ask.

Mugen-Ryu.note: In a fight in which the unit makes no follow-up attack, each attack of the round it lands is followed at once by one more with the weapon in hand, at half the Hit it comes to against that foe (rounded down), and by another for as long as each lands: 4 in a row at the most, ended by the first that misses or by the foe's fall. Each wears the weapon as any attack does. The attacks it adds begin no chain of their own and set off no attack in answer, and the forecast shows the round without them.

Short Tempered.note: In a fight the unit starts, its foe attacks first where it attacks at all, which the forecast shows; a fight an enemy starts is as it was. Against a foe with the same skill, or beside a skill that has the unit itself attack first, the round is as usual. Once an attack has landed on the unit in a fight, whatever it dealt, every attack it makes for the rest of that fight has +5 Might.

Hitobashira.note: An attack of the unit that defeats its foe restores the damage it dealt, which is no more than the HP the foe had left. "Until they are damaged for 25% or more of their HP" is read from the HP the unit is missing: it regains 3 HP as its turn starts while it has more than 75% of its maximum HP, and again once it is healed back above that.

Hard to Kill.note: +1 DEF and RES for every 3 HP the unit is missing, rounded down; in a fight, by the HP it has as the fight begins. While it is below half its maximum HP, an enemy that stands within 2 tiles of it cannot attack an ally of it within 2 tiles of it: the map offers no tile so near to attack from, and says why when such an ally is clicked. The unit itself can be attacked, and so can those allies from further away. Staves and skills are not attacks, and are not barred.

Senbonzakura.note: A tally kept on the unit for the rest of the map, as its Effect names no end: +1 STR, MAG, DEF and RES for each enemy it defeats, up to +9, and 1 less for each hit of an attack that deals it damage, never below 0. It counts from after the fight in which it changed.

Demon's Embrace.note: In a fight the unit starts while its foe, or the unit itself, is at or below 30% of its maximum HP as the fight begins: every hit of the unit in that fight restores the damage it dealt, which is no more than the HP the foe had left. What holds as the fight begins holds for all of it.

Haggle.note: In the Market of the Base the unit pays 10% less, on top of what Bargain and a Bargain Ring take off, and is paid 10% more for what it sells there or from its sheet; each price shown is the one that counts, rounded down, with where it comes from on hover. In the Creator its starting equipment costs it 10% less, which the armoury says, and handing a purchase back returns what was paid.

Income.note: 5 Gold as each of the unit's turns starts, and 1 Gold for each space it moved as that turn ends, the spaces of a move made after its Action included; a move that was taken back counts for nothing. Spaces are counted in a battle on the map. What it has given in this map is counted on the skill, and the world setting "Most Gold a map gives from a skill such as Income" holds it to that much a map; at 0 there is no limit. The Gold shows as a float over the unit, without a card.

Wealth Of Power.note: Using a Gem from the unit's pack asks first, then destroys it and is the unit's Action; its power lasts for the rest of the map and shows among the changes on the unit. A Gem whose power is already in effect is kept. Green: 5 HP as each turn starts. Red: +6 STR, +10 Critical. Blue: +20 Dodge. Purple: every hit of the unit Poisons, and every enemy next to it is Poisoned as its turn starts. White: what Charm and Solidarity give the allies within 3 spaces (+10 Hit and Dodge, +10 Critical and Critical Avoid). Pink: +5 LUK, and a third of its LUK with those 5, rounded down, to Hit and Dodge. Black: what Wrath and Heroism give at half HP or less (+50 Critical, +30 Skill Activation). Rainbow: double damage, +15 Hit, Dodge and Critical. A skill a Gem grants is not given twice to a unit that has it.

Make A Killing.note: By the Gold on the unit's own sheet: +1 Hit for every 500, +1 Dodge for every 1,000, +1 Critical for every 1,500 and +1 damage for every 2,000, each rounded down. Attack is counted as damage.
